lessons.title: 最好的教育
lessons.daodu: 你觉得你在什么地方学到的东西最重要？来听听诺贝尔奖获得者的想法吧。
lessons.daoduEn: Where do you think you learned the most important things? Let's hear what a Nobel Prize winner thinks.

paras.zh: 有一年，75位诺贝尔奖获得者在巴黎聚会。有个记者问其中的一位：“在您的一生中，您认为最重要的东西是在哪所学校学到的呢？”
paras.py: Yǒu yì nián, 75 wèi Nuòbèi'ěr Jiǎng huòdézhě zài Bālí jùhuì. Yǒu gè jìzhě wèn qízhōng de yí wèi: “Zài nín de yìshēng zhōng, nín rènwéi zuì zhòngyào de dōngxi shì zài nǎ suǒ xuéxiào xuédào de ne?”
paras.en: One year, 75 Nobel Prize winners gathered in Paris. A reporter asked one of them: "In your whole life, at which school do you think you learned the most important things?"

paras.zh: 这位满头白发的诺贝尔奖获得者平静地回答：“是在幼儿园。”
paras.py: Zhè wèi mǎntóu báifà de Nuòbèi'ěr Jiǎng huòdézhě píngjìng de huídá: “Shì zài yòu'éryuán.”
paras.en: The white-haired Nobel Prize winner answered calmly: "In kindergarten."

paras.zh: 记者感到非常惊奇，又问：“为什么是在幼儿园呢？您认为您在幼儿园里学到了什么呢？”
paras.py: Jìzhě gǎndào fēicháng jīngqí, yòu wèn: “Wèishénme shì zài yòu'éryuán ne? Nín rènwéi nín zài yòu'éryuán li xuédàole shénme ne?”
paras.en: The reporter was very surprised and asked again: "Why kindergarten? What do you think you learned there?"

paras.zh: 老人微笑着回答：“在幼儿园里，我学到了很多很多。比如，把自己的东西分一半给小朋友们；不是自己的东西不要拿；东西要放整齐；饭前要洗手，午饭后要休息；做了错事要道歉；学习时要多思考。我认为，我学到的全部东西就是这些。”
paras.py: Lǎorén wēixiàozhe huídá: “Zài yòu'éryuán li, wǒ xuédàole hěn duō hěn duō. Bǐrú, bǎ zìjǐ de dōngxi fēn yíbàn gěi xiǎopéngyoumen; bú shì zìjǐ de dōngxi búyào ná; dōngxi yào fàng zhěngqí; fàn qián yào xǐ shǒu, wǔfàn hòu yào xiūxi; zuòle cuòshì yào dàoqiàn; xuéxí shí yào duō sīkǎo. Wǒ rènwéi, wǒ xuédào de quánbù dōngxi jiù shì zhèxiē.”
paras.en: The old man smiled and answered: "In kindergarten I learned a great many things. For example: share half of your things with the other children; don't take things that aren't yours; put things away neatly; wash your hands before meals and rest after lunch; say sorry when you do something wrong; think a lot when you study. I believe everything I've learned is just these things."

paras.zh: 老人一讲完，所有的人都站起来鼓掌。事实上，大多数科学家都认为，他们一生中学到的最重要的东西，就是幼儿园老师教给他们的好习惯。
paras.py: Lǎorén yì jiǎngwán, suǒyǒu de rén dōu zhàn qǐlai gǔzhǎng. Shìshí shang, dàduōshù kēxuéjiā dōu rènwéi, tāmen yìshēng zhōng xuédào de zuì zhòngyào de dōngxi, jiù shì yòu'éryuán lǎoshī jiāo gěi tāmen de hǎo xíguàn.
paras.en: As soon as the old man finished, everyone stood up and clapped. In fact, most scientists believe that the most important things they learned in their lives were the good habits their kindergarten teachers taught them.

points.name: 感到
points.eg: 记者感到非常惊奇。
points.egEn: The journalist felt very surprised.
points.zh: “感到”，动词。表示心里产生某种感觉，后面常跟形容词或表示心理的词语，如“感到高兴”“感到奇怪”。
points.enx: “感到” is a verb meaning “to feel”. It is usually followed by an adjective or a word of feeling, e.g. “感到高兴” (feel happy), “感到奇怪” (feel strange).
egs: （1）听到这个好消息，大家都感到非常高兴。
（2）第一次一个人出国，我感到有点儿紧张。

points.name: 事实上
points.eg: 事实上，大多数科学家都认为，他们一生中学到的最重要的东西，就是幼儿园老师教给他们的好习惯。
points.egEn: In fact, most scientists believe that the most important things they learned in their lives were the good habits their kindergarten teachers taught them.
points.zh: “事实上”，插入语，常用在句首。表示说出真实的情况，后面的内容常常是对前面说法的补充或纠正。
points.enx: “事实上” (in fact) is a parenthetical phrase, usually used at the beginning of a sentence. It introduces the real situation, often adding to or correcting what was said before.
egs: （1）很多人觉得汉字很难，事实上，只要方法对，学汉字并不难。
（2）他说自己不累，事实上，他已经两天没睡好觉了。

tip.title: 诺贝尔奖
tip.zh: 诺贝尔奖是以瑞典化学家阿尔弗雷德·诺贝尔的名字命名的。诺贝尔一生有很多发明，其中最有名的是炸药，他也因此积累了大量财富。1895年，他在遗嘱中决定，用自己的大部分财产设立一个基金，每年奖励在物理、化学、生理学或医学、文学与和平方面为人类作出巨大贡献的人。1901年，诺贝尔奖第一次颁发，1968年又增设了经济学奖。每年12月10日，也就是诺贝尔去世的纪念日，都会举行颁奖仪式。
tip.en: The Nobel Prize is named after the Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel. Nobel made many inventions in his lifetime, the most famous being dynamite, which brought him a great fortune. In his will of 1895 he decided to use most of his wealth to set up a fund that would reward, every year, people who had made great contributions to humanity in physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, literature and peace. The prizes were first awarded in 1901, and a prize in economics was added in 1968. The award ceremony is held every year on 10 December, the anniversary of Nobel's death.

lessons.title: 北京的四合院
lessons.daodu: 你去过北京的四合院吗？如果有机会，你一定要去看看。
lessons.daoduEn: Have you ever been to a siheyuan in Beijing? If you get the chance, you must go and see one.

paras.zh: 四合院是老北京人居住的主要建筑，在国内外都很有名。
paras.py: Sìhéyuàn shì lǎo Běijīngrén jūzhù de zhǔyào jiànzhù, zài guónèiwài dōu hěn yǒumíng.
paras.en: The siheyuan (courtyard house) was the main kind of home for old Beijing people, and it is famous both in China and abroad.

paras.zh: 北京四合院为什么有名呢？首先是因为它有六百多年的历史。从元朝开始，四合院就出现了。其次是它的构成非常特别，在中国传统住宅建筑中很有代表性。四合院的“四”是“东南西北”四面的意思，“合”是围在一起的意思。也就是说，四合院是由四面的房屋或院墙围成的，只要关上大门，四合院就和外面隔开了。
paras.py: Běijīng sìhéyuàn wèishénme yǒumíng ne? Shǒuxiān shì yīnwèi tā yǒu liùbǎi duō nián de lìshǐ. Cóng Yuáncháo kāishǐ, sìhéyuàn jiù chūxiàn le. Qícì shì tā de gòuchéng fēicháng tèbié, zài Zhōngguó chuántǒng zhùzhái jiànzhù zhōng hěn yǒu dàibiǎoxìng. Sìhéyuàn de “sì” shì “dōng nán xī běi” sì miàn de yìsi, “hé” shì wéi zài yìqǐ de yìsi. Yě jiù shì shuō, sìhéyuàn shì yóu sì miàn de fángwū huò yuànqiáng wéichéng de, zhǐyào guānshang dàmén, sìhéyuàn jiù hé wàimian gékāi le.
paras.en: Why is the Beijing siheyuan famous? First, because it has a history of more than six hundred years. Siheyuan appeared as early as the Yuan Dynasty. Second, its structure is very special, and it is typical of traditional Chinese homes. The "si" (four) in siheyuan means the four sides - east, south, west and north - and "he" means enclosed together. In other words, a siheyuan is surrounded by houses or walls on four sides; once you close the front gate, it is cut off from the outside.

paras.zh: 几百年来，北京人就在这样的四合院中生活。过去，一个四合院只住一家人。后来，一座四合院住进了两家、三家……有的四合院甚至住了十几家人，成为了现在北京人所说的“大杂院儿”。大杂院儿里邻居的亲密关系是许多老北京人永远无法忘记的。
paras.py: Jǐ bǎi nián lái, Běijīngrén jiù zài zhèyàng de sìhéyuàn zhōng shēnghuó. Guòqù, yí gè sìhéyuàn zhǐ zhù yì jiā rén. Hòulái, yí zuò sìhéyuàn zhùjìnle liǎng jiā, sān jiā... yǒu de sìhéyuàn shènzhì zhùle shí jǐ jiā rén, chéngwéile xiànzài Běijīngrén suǒ shuō de “dàzáyuànr”. Dàzáyuànr li línjū de qīnmì guānxi shì xǔduō lǎo Běijīngrén yǒngyuǎn wúfǎ wàngjì de.
paras.en: For hundreds of years, Beijing people lived in siheyuan like this. In the past, one siheyuan housed just one family. Later, two or three families moved into one siheyuan... some even held more than ten families, becoming what Beijing people now call a "dazayuanr" (a crowded shared courtyard). Many old Beijingers will never forget the close ties between neighbors in these courtyards.

paras.zh: 四合院之所以有名，还因为它虽然是居住建筑，但是却有着很深的中国传统文化。目前，典型的四合院越来越少。为了让这种具有中国特色的民族建筑保存下来，北京已经开始保护四合院了。
paras.py: Sìhéyuàn zhīsuǒyǐ yǒumíng, hái yīnwèi tā suīrán shì jūzhù jiànzhù, dànshì què yǒuzhe hěn shēn de Zhōngguó chuántǒng wénhuà. Mùqián, diǎnxíng de sìhéyuàn yuè lái yuè shǎo. Wèile ràng zhè zhǒng jùyǒu Zhōngguó tèsè de mínzú jiànzhù bǎocún xiàlai, Běijīng yǐjīng kāishǐ bǎohù sìhéyuàn le.
paras.en: Siheyuan are also famous because, although they are homes, they carry deep traditional Chinese culture. Today there are fewer and fewer typical siheyuan. To preserve this kind of building with Chinese characteristics, Beijing has begun protecting them.

points.name: 所说的
points.eg: 有的四合院甚至住了十几家人，成为了现在北京人所说的“大杂院儿”。
points.egEn: Some siheyuan even housed a dozen or more families, becoming what Beijingers now call “dazayuanr” (multi-household compounds).
points.zh: “所说的”用在名词前，“A所说的B”表示“A说的那个B”，常用来引出某种特别的叫法或说法。
points.enx: “所说的” is placed before a noun. “A所说的B” means “what A calls B” or “the B that A talks about”. It often introduces a special name or expression.
egs: （1）这就是老北京人所说的“胡同”。
（2）他就是你上次所说的那位汉语老师吗？

points.name: 无法
points.eg: 大杂院儿里邻居的亲密关系是许多老北京人永远无法忘记的。
points.egEn: The close relationships between neighbours in the dazayuanr are something many old Beijingers can never forget.
points.zh: “无法”，动词，意思是“没有办法”，后面跟动词或动词短语，多用于书面语。
points.enx: “无法” means “to be unable to; to have no way to”. It is followed by a verb or verb phrase and is used mostly in written Chinese.
egs: （1）雨下得太大了，我们无法按时出发。
（2）这么多工作，一个人无法在一天内做完。

tip.title: 四合院与胡同
tip.zh: 在北京，四合院和胡同是分不开的。一座座四合院排列在一起，院与院之间留出的通道就是胡同。一般认为，“胡同”这个词是元朝时从蒙古语传来的。北京的胡同有宽有窄，名字也很有意思，有的用人名，有的用地名，有的用商品名。过去，胡同里的邻居们互相帮助，孩子们在胡同里一起玩耍，人和人之间充满了人情味。所以人们常说，胡同和四合院是老北京文化的“根”。
tip.en: In Beijing, siheyuan and hutong cannot be separated. Siheyuan stand side by side, and the lanes left between them are the hutong. It is generally believed that the word “hutong” came from Mongolian during the Yuan Dynasty. Beijing's hutong may be wide or narrow, and their names are interesting: some are named after people, some after places and some after goods. In the past, neighbours in a hutong helped one another and children played together in the lanes, so life there was full of warmth. That is why people often say that hutong and siheyuan are the “roots” of old Beijing culture.

lessons.title: 好一朵茉莉花
lessons.daodu: 现在，很多外国朋友都知道《茉莉花》这首中国歌曲。我们一起来听听吧。
lessons.daoduEn: Today many foreign friends know the Chinese song “Jasmine Flower”. Let's listen to it together.

paras.zh: 好一朵茉莉花，好一朵茉莉花，
paras.py: Hǎo yì duǒ mòlìhuā, hǎo yì duǒ mòlìhuā,
paras.en: What a lovely jasmine flower, what a lovely jasmine flower,

paras.zh: 满园花草，香也香不过它。
paras.py: Mǎn yuán huācǎo, xiāng yě xiāng bú guò tā.
paras.en: Of all the flowers in the garden, none smells as sweet as it.

paras.zh: 我有心采一朵戴，
paras.py: Wǒ yǒuxīn cǎi yì duǒ dài,
paras.en: I'd like to pick one to wear,

paras.zh: 看花的人儿要将我骂。
paras.py: Kàn huā de rénr yào jiāng wǒ mà.
paras.en: But the garden keeper would scold me.

paras.zh: 好一朵茉莉花，好一朵茉莉花，
paras.py: Hǎo yì duǒ mòlìhuā, hǎo yì duǒ mòlìhuā,
paras.en: What a lovely jasmine flower, what a lovely jasmine flower,

paras.zh: 茉莉花开，雪也白不过它。
paras.py: Mòlìhuā kāi, xuě yě bái bú guò tā.
paras.en: When the jasmine blooms, not even snow is whiter.

paras.zh: 我有心采一朵戴，
paras.py: Wǒ yǒuxīn cǎi yì duǒ dài,
paras.en: I'd like to pick one to wear,

paras.zh: 又怕旁人笑话。
paras.py: Yòu pà pángrén xiàohua.
paras.en: But I'm afraid others would laugh at me.

paras.zh: 好一朵茉莉花，好一朵茉莉花，
paras.py: Hǎo yì duǒ mòlìhuā, hǎo yì duǒ mòlìhuā,
paras.en: What a lovely jasmine flower, what a lovely jasmine flower,

paras.zh: 满园花开，比也比不过它。
paras.py: Mǎn yuán huā kāi, bǐ yě bǐ bú guò tā.
paras.en: Of all the flowers blooming in the garden, none can compare with it.

paras.zh: 我有心采一朵戴，
paras.py: Wǒ yǒuxīn cǎi yì duǒ dài,
paras.en: I'd like to pick one to wear,

paras.zh: 又怕来年不发芽。
paras.py: Yòu pà láinián bù fāyá.
paras.en: But I'm afraid it won't sprout again next year.

paras.zh: 《茉莉花》是中国最有名的民歌之一。这首民歌通过赞美茉莉花，来表现男女之间纯洁美好的感情。
paras.py: “Mòlìhuā” shì Zhōngguó zuì yǒumíng de míngē zhī yī. Zhè shǒu míngē tōngguò zànměi mòlìhuā, lái biǎoxiàn nán nǚ zhījiān chúnjié měihǎo de gǎnqíng.
paras.en: "Jasmine Flower" is one of China's most famous folk songs. By praising the jasmine flower, it expresses the pure and beautiful love between a man and a woman.

paras.zh: 1804年，有个英国人把这首歌收进了他的书中。于是，《茉莉花》成为了中国第一首通过书流传到国外的民歌。1926年，著名的意大利音乐家普契尼（Giacomo Puccini，1858—1924）的歌剧《图兰朵》（Turandot）开始在意大利演出，并获得巨大成功。由于普契尼把《茉莉花》作为这部歌剧的主要音乐之一，所以随着这个歌剧的流传，“茉莉花”的芳香也飘到了世界各地。
paras.py: 1804 nián, yǒu gè Yīngguórén bǎ zhè shǒu gē shōujìnle tā de shū zhōng. Yúshì, “Mòlìhuā” chéngwéile Zhōngguó dì-yī shǒu tōngguò shū liúchuán dào guówài de míngē. 1926 nián, zhùmíng de Yìdàlì yīnyuèjiā Pǔqìní (Giacomo Puccini, 1858—1924) de gējù “Túlánduǒ” (Turandot) kāishǐ zài Yìdàlì yǎnchū, bìng huòdé jùdà chénggōng. Yóuyú Pǔqìní bǎ “Mòlìhuā” zuòwéi zhè bù gējù de zhǔyào yīnyuè zhī yī, suǒyǐ suízhe zhège gējù de liúchuán, “mòlìhuā” de fāngxiāng yě piāodàole shìjiè gè dì.
paras.en: In 1804, an Englishman included this song in his book. So "Jasmine Flower" became the first Chinese folk song to spread abroad through a book. In 1926, the opera Turandot by the famous Italian composer Giacomo Puccini (1858-1924) opened in Italy and was a huge success. Because Puccini used "Jasmine Flower" as one of the opera's main melodies, the fragrance of the "jasmine" drifted all over the world as the opera spread.

paras.zh: 其实，《茉莉花》本来有三段歌词，分别唱的是茉莉花、金银花和玫瑰花。1957年，一位音乐家把这首歌从唱三种花改成只唱茉莉花，就成了我们今天听到的这首《茉莉花》。现在中国的重大活动中经常会演唱《茉莉花》这首歌。
paras.py: Qíshí, “Mòlìhuā” běnlái yǒu sān duàn gēcí, fēnbié chàng de shì mòlìhuā, jīnyínhuā hé méiguihuā. 1957 nián, yí wèi yīnyuèjiā bǎ zhè shǒu gē cóng chàng sān zhǒng huā gǎichéng zhǐ chàng mòlìhuā, jiù chéngle wǒmen jīntiān tīngdào de zhè shǒu “Mòlìhuā”. Xiànzài Zhōngguó de zhòngdà huódòng zhōng jīngcháng huì yǎnchàng “Mòlìhuā” zhè shǒu gē.
paras.en: In fact, "Jasmine Flower" originally had three verses, about the jasmine, the honeysuckle and the rose. In 1957, a musician changed the song from singing about three flowers to singing only about the jasmine, and that became the "Jasmine Flower" we hear today. Now the song is often performed at major events in China.

points.name: 通过
points.eg: 这首民歌通过赞美茉莉花，来表现男女之间纯洁美好的感情。
points.egEn: By praising the jasmine flower, this folk song expresses the pure and beautiful feelings between a man and a woman.
points.zh: “通过”，介词，表示以某种方式或手段达到目的，常用格式是“通过……（来）……”。
points.enx: “通过” is a preposition meaning “by means of; through”. It introduces the way or method used to reach a goal, often in the pattern “通过……（来）……”.
egs: （1）我们通过网络认识了很多新朋友。
（2）他通过自己的努力，终于考上了理想的大学。

points.name: 本来
points.eg: 《茉莉花》本来有三段歌词。
points.egEn: “Jasmine Flower” originally had three verses.
points.zh: “本来”，副词，表示“原先、先前”，说明以前的情况，常常暗示后来发生了变化。
points.enx: “本来” is an adverb meaning “originally; at first”. It describes an earlier situation and often implies that things changed later.
egs: （1）我本来打算周末去爬山，后来因为下雨没去成。
（2）这条街本来很安静，现在开了很多饭馆，热闹多了。

think: “茉莉花”的芳香是怎么飘到世界各地的？
现在的《茉莉花》和原来有什么不同？

tf.q: 1926年意大利人普契尼的歌剧《茉莉花》开始演出。
以前这首歌中有三种花，现在只有茉莉花一种花。
现在中国的重大活动中经常会使用《茉莉花》这首歌曲。

mc.q: 《茉莉花》首先流传到了（ ）。
最早的《茉莉花》里没有（ ）。

tip.title: 茉莉花
tip.zh: 茉莉花是一种常绿小灌木，叶子翠绿，花朵洁白，夏天开得最多。茉莉花的香气清新淡雅，很多人喜欢在家里种上一盆，既可以观赏，又能让屋子里充满花香。茉莉花还可以用来做香料和食品。中国人最熟悉的是茉莉花茶：把茶叶和新鲜的茉莉花放在一起，让茶叶吸收花的香味，就做成了香气浓郁的花茶。福州的茉莉花茶非常有名。另外，茉莉花还是菲律宾的国花。
tip.en: Jasmine is a small evergreen shrub with bright green leaves and pure white flowers, which bloom most in summer. Its fragrance is fresh and delicate, so many people like to keep a pot at home: it is pleasant to look at and fills the room with its scent. Jasmine is also used in perfumes and food. What Chinese people know best is jasmine tea: tea leaves are put together with fresh jasmine flowers so that they absorb the scent, producing a richly fragrant flower tea. The jasmine tea of Fuzhou is especially famous. Jasmine is also the national flower of the Philippines.

lessons.title: 倒茶的礼貌
lessons.daodu: 你喜欢喝茶吗？你知道礼貌的倒茶方法吗？
lessons.daoduEn: Do you like drinking tea? Do you know the polite way to pour it?

paras.zh: 喝茶对人的身体有很多好处。中国是茶叶的故乡，人们很早以前就有喝茶的习惯。同时，用茶招待客人也是中国人的一个重要礼节。
paras.py: Hē chá duì rén de shēntǐ yǒu hěn duō hǎochù. Zhōngguó shì cháyè de gùxiāng, rénmen hěn zǎo yǐqián jiù yǒu hē chá de xíguàn. Tóngshí, yòng chá zhāodài kèrén yě shì Zhōngguórén de yí gè zhòngyào lǐjié.
paras.en: Drinking tea is very good for your health. China is the home of tea, and people there have had the habit of drinking tea since long ago. Serving guests tea is also an important custom of Chinese courtesy.

paras.zh: 人们对喝茶的方法非常讲究，倒茶也有一些需要注意的地方。首先，茶杯要非常干净。倒茶之前，要认真地用水洗茶杯，最好用开水烫一下。这样不但卫生，而且对客人也是一种礼貌。
paras.py: Rénmen duì hē chá de fāngfǎ fēicháng jiǎngjiu, dào chá yě yǒu yìxiē xūyào zhùyì de dìfang. Shǒuxiān, chábēi yào fēicháng gānjìng. Dào chá zhīqián, yào rènzhēn de yòng shuǐ xǐ chábēi, zuìhǎo yòng kāishuǐ tàng yíxià. Zhèyàng búdàn wèishēng, érqiě duì kèrén yě shì yì zhǒng lǐmào.
paras.en: People are very particular about how they drink tea, and there are some things to pay attention to when pouring it. First, the teacups must be very clean. Before pouring, wash the cups carefully, ideally rinsing them with boiling water. This is not only hygienic but also polite to the guest.

paras.zh: 其次，茶叶的多少要合适。茶叶多，茶的味道就会浓一些；茶叶少，茶的味道就会淡一些。所以，最好先问问客人喜欢喝浓茶还是淡茶，然后按照客人的习惯放茶叶。再说水，无论是大茶杯还是小茶杯，水都不能倒太满或太少。
paras.py: Qícì, cháyè de duōshao yào héshì. Cháyè duō, chá de wèidao jiù huì nóng yìxiē; cháyè shǎo, chá de wèidao jiù huì dàn yìxiē. Suǒyǐ, zuìhǎo xiān wènwen kèrén xǐhuan hē nóng chá háishi dàn chá, ránhòu ànzhào kèrén de xíguàn fàng cháyè. Zài shuō shuǐ, wúlùn shì dà chábēi háishi xiǎo chábēi, shuǐ dōu bù néng dào tài mǎn huò tài shǎo.
paras.en: Second, use the right amount of tea leaves. More leaves make the tea stronger; fewer make it weaker. So it's best to first ask whether the guest likes strong or weak tea, then add leaves to suit them. As for the water, whether the cup is big or small, don't fill it too full or too little.

paras.zh: 再次，端茶要有礼貌。按照中国的传统习惯，茶杯应该用双手端。其中一只手拿着茶杯，另一只手托住茶杯下面，这样把茶端给客人才是最有礼貌的。
paras.py: Zàicì, duān chá yào yǒu lǐmào. Ànzhào Zhōngguó de chuántǒng xíguàn, chábēi yīnggāi yòng shuāngshǒu duān. Qízhōng yì zhī shǒu názhe chábēi, lìng yì zhī shǒu tuōzhù chábēi xiàmian, zhèyàng bǎ chá duān gěi kèrén cái shì zuì yǒu lǐmào de.
paras.en: Third, serve the tea politely. By Chinese tradition, the cup should be held with both hands: one hand holds the cup and the other supports its bottom. Handing tea to a guest this way is the most polite.

paras.zh: 最后，加水也要有礼貌。如果客人茶杯里的茶快喝完了，要及时给客人加水。加水的时候要先给客人加，再给自己加。这样做也表示对客人的尊敬。
paras.py: Zuìhòu, jiā shuǐ yě yào yǒu lǐmào. Rúguǒ kèrén chábēi li de chá kuài hēwán le, yào jíshí gěi kèrén jiā shuǐ. Jiā shuǐ de shíhou yào xiān gěi kèrén jiā, zài gěi zìjǐ jiā. Zhèyàng zuò yě biǎoshì duì kèrén de zūnjìng.
paras.en: Finally, top up the water politely too. If the guest's tea is almost finished, add more water right away. Top up the guest's cup first and then your own. This also shows respect for the guest.

points.name: 讲究
points.en: pay attention to, be particular about
points.eg: 人们对喝茶的方法非常讲究，倒茶也有一些需要注意的地方。
points.egEn: People are very particular about the way they drink tea, and there are also some things to pay attention to when pouring it.
points.zh: “讲究”，动词，表示对某方面很重视，要求很高，常用格式是“对……很讲究”。也可以作名词，如“很有讲究”，表示值得注意的方法或道理。
points.enx: “讲究” is a verb meaning “to pay great attention to; to be particular about”, often in the pattern “对……很讲究”. It can also be a noun, as in “很有讲究”, meaning “something that requires care or know-how”.
egs: （1）她对穿衣服很讲究，每天都打扮得很漂亮。
（2）我爷爷对吃很讲究，菜一定要新鲜。

points.name: 按照
points.eg: 按照中国的传统习惯，茶杯应该用双手端。
points.egEn: According to traditional Chinese custom, a teacup should be served with both hands.
points.zh: “按照”，介词，表示以某种标准、规定或习惯为根据去做，后面常跟“规定、要求、习惯、计划”等名词。
points.enx: “按照” is a preposition meaning “according to”. It shows that something is done on the basis of a standard, rule or custom, and is often followed by nouns such as 规定, 要求, 习惯 and 计划.
egs: （1）请大家按照老师的要求完成作业。
（2）我们按照原来的计划，下个星期去上海旅行。

think: 作者觉得喝茶有什么好处？
你知道应该怎样端茶给客人吗？

tf.q: 倒茶前最好先洗一下茶杯。
给客人倒茶，应该把水倒满。
给客人端茶，应该两只手同时拿着茶杯。
加水时，应该先给客人加。
中国是茶叶的故乡。
为了表示尊敬客人，就要多放茶叶。

tip.title: 中国的龙井茶
tip.zh: 中国是世界上最早种茶和喝茶的国家，茶叶的种类非常多，一般可以分为绿茶、红茶、乌龙茶、白茶、黄茶和黑茶六大类。在众多名茶中，龙井茶是最有名的绿茶之一。龙井茶产于浙江杭州西湖一带，所以又叫“西湖龙井”。它有“色绿、香郁、味甘、形美”四个特点，被人们称为“四绝”。清明节以前采摘的龙井叫“明前茶”，数量少、质量好，价格也最贵。
tip.en: China was the first country in the world to grow and drink tea, and it has a great many kinds of tea, generally divided into six groups: green, black (red), oolong, white, yellow and dark tea. Among the many famous teas, Longjing is one of the best-known green teas. It is grown around West Lake in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, so it is also called “West Lake Longjing”. It is praised for four qualities—green colour, rich aroma, sweet taste and beautiful shape—known as the “four wonders”. Longjing picked before the Qingming Festival, called “pre-Qingming tea”, is scarce and of the best quality, and it is also the most expensive.

lessons.title: 铁杵磨成针
lessons.en: Grinding an Iron Rod into a Needle
lessons.daodu: 一个人要成功，最需要什么？答案也许有很多。但做好任何事情都需要坚持，需要努力。
lessons.daoduEn: What does a person need most in order to succeed? There may be many answers. But doing anything well takes perseverance and hard work.

paras.zh: 唐代大诗人李白小时候不喜欢上学，常常逃课，到街上去玩儿。
paras.py: Tángdài dà shīrén Lǐ Bái xiǎo shíhou bù xǐhuan shàngxué, chángcháng táokè, dào jiē shang qù wánr.
paras.en: When the great Tang Dynasty poet Li Bai was a child, he didn't like going to school. He often skipped class to go and play in the streets.

paras.zh: 一天，李白又没有去上学，跑到城外去玩儿。看着城外的美景，李白心想：每天在屋里读书多没意思，从此玩儿多好啊！
paras.py: Yì tiān, Lǐ Bái yòu méiyǒu qù shàngxué, pǎodào chéng wài qù wánr. Kànzhe chéng wài de měijǐng, Lǐ Bái xīn xiǎng: Měi tiān zài wū li dúshū duō méi yìsi, cóngcǐ wánr duō hǎo a!
paras.en: One day, Li Bai skipped school again and ran outside the city to play. Looking at the beautiful scenery, he thought: "How boring it is to study indoors every day. How nice it would be to just play from now on!"

paras.zh: 他走着走着，看见一个白发的老婆婆，正在磨一根非常粗的铁杵。李白走过去问：“老婆婆，您在做什么？”
paras.py: Tā zǒuzhe zǒuzhe, kànjiàn yí gè báifà de lǎopópo, zhèngzài mó yì gēn fēicháng cū de tiěchǔ. Lǐ Bái zǒu guòqu wèn: “Lǎopópo, nín zài zuò shénme?”
paras.en: As he walked along, he saw a white-haired old woman grinding a very thick iron rod. Li Bai went over and asked, "Granny, what are you doing?"

paras.zh: “我要把这根铁杵磨成一根绣花针。”老婆婆对李白笑了笑，又低下头继续磨。
paras.py: “Wǒ yào bǎ zhè gēn tiěchǔ móchéng yì gēn xiùhuāzhēn.” Lǎopópo duì Lǐ Bái xiàole xiào, yòu dīxia tóu jìxù mó.
paras.en: "I'm going to grind this iron rod into an embroidery needle." The old woman smiled at Li Bai, then lowered her head and went on grinding.

paras.zh: “绣花针？”李白又问，“是缝衣服用的绣花针吗？”
paras.py: “Xiùhuāzhēn?” Lǐ Bái yòu wèn, “Shì féng yīfu yòng de xiùhuāzhēn ma?”
paras.en: "An embroidery needle?" Li Bai asked again. "The kind of needle used for sewing clothes?"

paras.zh: “当然！”
paras.py: “Dāngrán!”
paras.en: "Of course!"

paras.zh: “可是，铁杵这么粗，什么时候才能磨成细细的绣花针呢？”
paras.py: “Kěshì, tiěchǔ zhème cū, shénme shíhou cái néng móchéng xìxì de xiùhuāzhēn ne?”
paras.en: "But the iron rod is so thick. When will it ever become a thin little needle?"

paras.zh: 老婆婆反问李白：“滴水可以穿石，铁杵为什么不能磨成绣花针呢？”
paras.py: Lǎopópo fǎnwèn Lǐ Bái: “Dī shuǐ kěyǐ chuān shí, tiěchǔ wèishénme bù néng móchéng xiùhuāzhēn ne?”
paras.en: The old woman asked Li Bai in return: "Dripping water can wear through stone. Why can't an iron rod be ground into a needle?"

paras.zh: “可是，您的年纪这么大了……”
paras.py: “Kěshì, nín de niánjì zhème dà le...”
paras.en: "But you're so old..."

paras.zh: “只要我比别人更努力，就没有做不到的事情。”
paras.py: “Zhǐyào wǒ bǐ biérén gèng nǔlì, jiù méiyǒu zuò bú dào de shìqing.”
paras.en: "As long as I work harder than others, there is nothing I can't do."

paras.zh: 老婆婆的话让李白很惭愧。回家后，他再没有逃过课，每天学习都特别用功，终于成为一名伟大的诗人。
paras.py: Lǎopópo de huà ràng Lǐ Bái hěn cánkuì. Huí jiā hòu, tā zài méiyǒu táoguo kè, měi tiān xuéxí dōu tèbié yònggōng, zhōngyú chéngwéi yì míng wěidà de shīrén.
paras.en: The old woman's words made Li Bai feel ashamed. After he went home, he never skipped class again. He studied extremely hard every day and finally became a great poet.

paras.zh: 这个故事告诉我们：无论做什么事情，只有不停地努力，才会成功。
paras.py: Zhège gùshi gàosu wǒmen: Wúlùn zuò shénme shìqing, zhǐyǒu bù tíng de nǔlì, cái huì chénggōng.
paras.en: This story tells us: whatever you do, only by working hard without stopping will you succeed.

points.name: 到……去……
points.eg: 唐代大诗人李白小时候不喜欢上学，常常逃课，到街上去玩儿。
points.egEn: When he was a boy, the great Tang Dynasty poet Li Bai didn't like going to school. He often skipped classes and went out into the streets to play.
points.zh: “到+地方+去+动词”表示去某个地方做某事，“去”后面的动词说明去的目的。
points.enx: The pattern “到 + place + 去 + verb” means “to go somewhere to do something”; the verb after 去 shows the purpose.
egs: （1）下课以后，我们到图书馆去看书吧。
（2）周末他常常到公园去跑步。

points.name: 为什么
points.eg: 滴水可以穿石，铁杵为什么不能磨成绣花针呢？
points.egEn: Dripping water can wear through a stone—why can't an iron pestle be ground into an embroidery needle?
points.zh: “为什么……呢？”在这里是反问句，不是真的提问，而是用问句的形式表示肯定的意思，语气更强。
points.enx: Here “为什么……呢？” forms a rhetorical question. It does not ask for an answer but expresses an affirmative meaning more strongly: “Why can't an iron pestle be ground into a needle?” means “Of course it can.”
egs: （1）别人能学会，我为什么不能学会呢？
（2）这么好的机会，你为什么不试试呢？

think: 李白小时候喜欢上学吗？
老婆婆的话对李白有什么影响？
这个故事说明了什么？

tf.q: 李白小时候每天都去上学，从来不去街上玩儿。
老婆婆要把铁杵磨成做衣服用的针。
李白觉得老婆婆要做的事情很简单。

mc.q: 李白觉得老婆婆不能成功，不是因为（ ）。
李白听了老婆婆的话，（ ）。

tip.title: 唐代的大诗人李白
tip.titleEn: Li Bai—a Great Poet of the Tang Dynasty
tip.zh: 李白（701—762）是唐代最伟大的诗人之一，被人们称为“诗仙”。他年轻时就离开家乡，游历了中国的许多名山大川，写下了大量优美的诗歌。李白的诗想象丰富、感情奔放、语言自然，充满了浪漫主义色彩。现在保存下来的李白诗歌有九百多首，其中《静夜思》“床前明月光，疑是地上霜。举头望明月，低头思故乡”，几乎每个中国人都会背。他和另一位大诗人杜甫被并称为“李杜”。
tip.en: Li Bai (701–762) was one of the greatest poets of the Tang Dynasty and is known as the “Immortal of Poetry”. He left his hometown when he was young, travelled to many of China's famous mountains and rivers, and wrote a great number of beautiful poems. His poetry is full of imagination, bold feeling and natural language, with a strongly romantic spirit. More than nine hundred of his poems survive today. Almost every Chinese person can recite his “Quiet Night Thoughts”: “Before my bed the moonlight gleams, like frost upon the ground. I raise my head to view the moon, then lower it, thinking of home.” He and the other great poet Du Fu are together called “Li-Du”.

lessons.title: 请为夸奖道歉
lessons.daodu: 美丽的外貌不是个人的本领。通过努力取得成就才是值得夸奖的。
lessons.daoduEn: Good looks are not a personal ability. Only achievements gained through hard work deserve praise.

paras.zh: 朋友给我讲过这样一个故事。
paras.py: Péngyou gěi wǒ jiǎngguo zhèyàng yí gè gùshi.
paras.en: A friend once told me this story.

paras.zh: 他到一个国家访问，周末到一位教授家中做客。进屋看到教授五岁的小女儿，满头金发，漂亮的眼睛像海水一样蓝。收下朋友带去的中国礼物后，小女孩儿微笑道谢，朋友禁不住夸奖说：“你长得这么漂亮，真是可爱极了！”
paras.py: Tā dào yí gè guójiā fǎngwèn, zhōumò dào yí wèi jiàoshòu jiā zhōng zuòkè. Jìn wū kàndào jiàoshòu wǔ suì de xiǎo nǚ'ér, mǎntóu jīnfà, piàoliang de yǎnjing xiàng hǎishuǐ yíyàng lán. Shōuxia péngyou dài qù de Zhōngguó lǐwù hòu, xiǎo nǚháir wēixiào dàoxiè, péngyou jīnbuzhù kuājiǎng shuō: “Nǐ zhǎng de zhème piàoliang, zhēn shì kě'ài jí le!”
paras.en: He was visiting a country, and one weekend he was a guest at a professor's home. Inside, he saw the professor's five-year-old daughter, with golden hair and beautiful eyes as blue as the sea. After accepting the Chinese gift my friend had brought, the little girl smiled and said thank you. My friend couldn't help praising her: "You're so pretty - you're absolutely adorable!"

paras.zh: 教授当时没有说什么，但是女儿走了之后，她变得严肃起来，“你伤害了我的女儿，你要向她道歉。”朋友特别吃惊：“我是在夸奖她，怎么会伤害她呢？”教授解释：“你是因为她的漂亮而夸奖她，但她的外貌取决于我和她父亲，和她的努力没有关系。可孩子还很小，不会明白。你的夸奖会让她认为这是她的本领。如果她认为漂亮值得骄傲，就会看不起不太好看的孩子。”教授接着说：“其实，你可以夸奖她的微笑和有礼貌，这是她自己努力的结果。所以，请为你刚才的夸奖道歉。”
paras.py: Jiàoshòu dāngshí méiyǒu shuō shénme, dànshì nǚ'ér zǒule zhīhòu, tā biàn de yánsù qǐlai, “Nǐ shānghàile wǒ de nǚ'ér, nǐ yào xiàng tā dàoqiàn.” Péngyou tèbié chījīng: “Wǒ shì zài kuājiǎng tā, zěnme huì shānghài tā ne?” Jiàoshòu jiěshì: “Nǐ shì yīnwèi tā de piàoliang ér kuājiǎng tā, dàn tā de wàimào qǔjué yú wǒ hé tā fùqin, hé tā de nǔlì méiyǒu guānxi. Kě háizi hái hěn xiǎo, bú huì míngbai. Nǐ de kuājiǎng huì ràng tā rènwéi zhè shì tā de běnlǐng. Rúguǒ tā rènwéi piàoliang zhíde jiāo'ào, jiù huì kànbuqǐ bú tài hǎokàn de háizi.” Jiàoshòu jiēzhe shuō: “Qíshí, nǐ kěyǐ kuājiǎng tā de wēixiào hé yǒu lǐmào, zhè shì tā zìjǐ nǔlì de jiéguǒ. Suǒyǐ, qǐng wèi nǐ gāngcái de kuājiǎng dàoqiàn.”
paras.en: The professor said nothing at the time, but after her daughter left, she became serious: "You've hurt my daughter. You need to apologize to her." My friend was very surprised: "I was praising her - how could that hurt her?" The professor explained: "You praised her because she is pretty, but her looks come from her father and me; they have nothing to do with her own effort. She is still very young and won't understand. Your praise will make her think her looks are her own achievement. If she thinks being pretty is something to be proud of, she will look down on children who aren't so good-looking." The professor went on: "Actually, you could praise her smile and her good manners - those are the result of her own effort. So please apologize for the praise you just gave."

paras.zh: “后来呢？”我禁不住问朋友。
paras.py: “Hòulái ne?” Wǒ jīnbuzhù wèn péngyou.
paras.en: "And then?" I couldn't help asking my friend.

paras.zh: “后来，我就向教授的小女儿道了歉，同时表扬了她的微笑和有礼貌。”朋友说，“从那以后，每当我看到漂亮的孩子，我都会对自己说，不要夸奖她们的外貌，因为每一次不合适的夸奖，都可能伤害孩子。”
paras.py: “Hòulái, wǒ jiù xiàng jiàoshòu de xiǎo nǚ'ér dàole qiàn, tóngshí biǎoyángle tā de wēixiào hé yǒu lǐmào.” Péngyou shuō, “Cóng nà yǐhòu, měi dāng wǒ kàndào piàoliang de háizi, wǒ dōu huì duì zìjǐ shuō, búyào kuājiǎng tāmen de wàimào, yīnwèi měi yí cì bù héshì de kuājiǎng, dōu kěnéng shānghài háizi.”
paras.en: "Then I apologized to the professor's little daughter, and at the same time praised her smile and good manners," my friend said. "Since then, whenever I see a pretty child, I tell myself not to praise their looks, because every unsuitable compliment may hurt a child."

points.name: 禁不住
points.eg: 朋友禁不住夸奖说：“你长得这么漂亮，真是可爱极了！”
points.egEn: My friend couldn't help praising her: “You're so pretty—you're really adorable!”
points.zh: “禁不住”，动词，表示控制不住自己，不由自主地做某事，后面常跟动词短语，如“禁不住笑了起来”。
points.enx: “禁不住” means “can't help (doing something); can't hold oneself back”. It is usually followed by a verb phrase, e.g. “禁不住笑了起来” (couldn't help laughing).
egs: （1）听了他讲的笑话，大家禁不住大笑起来。
（2）看到妈妈寄来的信，她禁不住流下了眼泪。

points.name: 取决于
points.eg: 她的外貌取决于我和她父亲。
points.egEn: Her looks depend on her father and me.
points.zh: “取决于”，动词，表示某事由某方面的情况决定，“A取决于B”就是“A由B决定”，多用于书面语。
points.enx: “取决于” means “to depend on; to be decided by”. “A取决于B” means “A is determined by B”. It is mostly used in written Chinese.
egs: （1）比赛能不能举行，取决于明天的天气。
（2）一个人能不能成功，主要取决于他自己的努力。

points.name: 值得
points.eg: 如果她认为漂亮值得骄傲，就会看不起不太好看的孩子。
points.egEn: If she thinks being pretty is something to be proud of, she will look down on children who are not so good-looking.
points.zh: “值得”，动词，表示这样做有意义、有价值，后面常跟动词或动词短语，如“值得一看”“值得骄傲”。
points.enx: “值得” means “to be worth (doing); to deserve”. It is often followed by a verb or verb phrase, e.g. “值得一看” (worth seeing), “值得骄傲” (something to be proud of).
egs: （1）这本书写得很好，值得一看。
（2）他一直热心帮助有困难的人，值得我们学习。

think: 教授为什么让“我”向小女孩儿道歉？
“我”为什么夸奖那个小女孩儿？
你同意教授的观点吗？

tf.q: 教授认为夸奖孩子的外貌对孩子没有好处。
教授认为朋友应该夸奖孩子的礼貌。
孩子的外貌和她自己的努力没有关系。
从那以后，朋友不再夸奖孩子的外貌了。

tip.title: 合适地夸奖
tip.zh: 夸奖可以让孩子感到快乐、增加自信，但是夸奖也要讲究方法。很多教育专家认为，夸奖孩子最好夸具体的行为和努力的过程，比如“你今天练习得很认真”“你主动帮助了同学”，而不是只说“你真聪明”“你真漂亮”。因为外貌和天生的条件不是孩子自己努力的结果，过多地夸奖这些，可能会让孩子变得骄傲，或者害怕失败。合适的夸奖能让孩子明白：只要努力，就能做得更好。
tip.en: Praise can make children happy and build their confidence, but it should be given in the right way. Many educators believe it is best to praise specific actions and the effort a child makes—for example, “You practised really carefully today” or “You helped your classmate without being asked”—rather than just saying “You're so clever” or “You're so pretty”. Looks and natural gifts are not the result of a child's own effort, and too much praise for them may make children proud or afraid of failure. Proper praise helps children understand that if they work hard, they can do better.

lessons.title: 王子赛马
lessons.daodu: 从相反的角度思考问题，有时会有不一样的效果。
lessons.daoduEn: Thinking about a problem from the opposite angle can sometimes produce a different result.

paras.zh: 一个国王有两个儿子。为了确定自己的继承人，他决定让两个儿子举行一场赛马比赛。但是这场比赛不是比谁跑得快，而是比谁的马最后到达终点。胜利者就成为继承人。
paras.py: Yí gè guówáng yǒu liǎng gè érzi. Wèile quèdìng zìjǐ de jìchéngrén, tā juédìng ràng liǎng gè érzi jǔxíng yì chǎng sàimǎ bǐsài. Dànshì zhè chǎng bǐsài bú shì bǐ shéi pǎo de kuài, ér shì bǐ shéi de mǎ zuìhòu dàodá zhōngdiǎn. Shènglìzhě jiù chéngwéi jìchéngrén.
paras.en: A king had two sons. To decide who would inherit his throne, he had his two sons hold a horse race. But this race wasn't about who ran fastest - it was about whose horse reached the finish line last. The winner would become the heir.

paras.zh: 他给了两个儿子不相上下的两匹马，让他们各挑一匹。比赛开始，两个儿子同时上路了。
paras.py: Tā gěile liǎng gè érzi bù xiāng shàng xià de liǎng pǐ mǎ, ràng tāmen gè tiāo yì pǐ. Bǐsài kāishǐ, liǎng gè érzi tóngshí shànglù le.
paras.en: He gave his sons two equally good horses and let each choose one. The race began, and the two sons set off at the same time.

paras.zh: 在路上，两个王子都很磨蹭，谁也不想快走。后来，两个王子都下马休息，不再走了。再后来，两个王子干脆躺下休息，看样子谁也不会走了。
paras.py: Zài lù shang, liǎng gè wángzǐ dōu hěn móceng, shéi yě bù xiǎng kuài zǒu. Hòulái, liǎng gè wángzǐ dōu xià mǎ xiūxi, bú zài zǒu le. Zài hòulái, liǎng gè wángzǐ gāncuì tǎngxia xiūxi, kàn yàngzi shéi yě bú huì zǒu le.
paras.en: On the way, both princes dawdled; neither wanted to go fast. Later, both got off their horses to rest and stopped moving. After that, they simply lay down, and it looked like neither of them would ever move again.

paras.zh: 这样下去也不是办法。小王子突然想出了一个主意，站起来就骑上了一匹马，跑了出去。大王子一愣，很快就明白了，于是也急急忙忙站起来，也骑上一匹马，去追小王子。
paras.py: Zhèyàng xiàqu yě bú shì bànfǎ. Xiǎo wángzǐ tūrán xiǎng chūle yí gè zhǔyi, zhàn qǐlai jiù qíshangle yì pǐ mǎ, pǎole chūqu. Dà wángzǐ yí lèng, hěn kuài jiù míngbai le, yúshì yě jíjímángmáng zhàn qǐlai, yě qíshang yì pǐ mǎ, qù zhuī xiǎo wángzǐ.
paras.en: Going on like this was no solution. The younger prince suddenly had an idea. He stood up, jumped onto a horse and galloped off. The older prince was stunned for a moment, but quickly understood. He hurried to his feet, jumped onto the other horse and chased after his brother.

paras.zh: 不用说，胜利者是小王子，他成了国王的继承人。
paras.py: Búyòng shuō, shènglìzhě shì xiǎo wángzǐ, tā chéngle guówáng de jìchéngrén.
paras.en: Needless to say, the younger prince won and became the king's heir.

paras.zh: 你知道小王子的好办法是什么吗？
paras.py: Nǐ zhīdào xiǎo wángzǐ de hǎo bànfǎ shì shénme ma?
paras.en: Do you know what the younger prince's clever trick was?

paras.zh: 答案就是逆向思维！他不是让自己的马跑得更慢，而是让哥哥的马跑得更快。怎么能让哥哥的马跑得更快呢？小王子骑上大王子的马跑起来，大王子的马先到终点，自己的马当然就后到了。
paras.py: Dá'àn jiù shì nìxiàng sīwéi! Tā bú shì ràng zìjǐ de mǎ pǎo de gèng màn, ér shì ràng gēge de mǎ pǎo de gèng kuài. Zěnme néng ràng gēge de mǎ pǎo de gèng kuài ne? Xiǎo wángzǐ qíshang dà wángzǐ de mǎ pǎo qǐlai, dà wángzǐ de mǎ xiān dào zhōngdiǎn, zìjǐ de mǎ dāngrán jiù hòu dào le.
paras.en: The answer is reverse thinking! Instead of making his own horse go slower, he made his brother's horse go faster. How? He rode off on his older brother's horse. His brother's horse reached the finish first, so of course his own horse arrived later.

points.name: 不相上下
points.eg: 他给了两个儿子不相上下的两匹马，让他们各挑一匹。
points.egEn: He gave his two sons two equally matched horses and let each of them pick one.
points.zh: “不相上下”，成语，表示两者差不多，分不出高低好坏，常作谓语或定语。
points.enx: “不相上下” is an idiom meaning “about the same; equally matched; hard to tell which is better”. It usually serves as a predicate or an attributive.
egs: （1）这两个班的汉语水平不相上下。
（2）他们俩的成绩不相上下，很难说谁更好。

points.name: 干脆
points.eg: 两个王子干脆躺下休息，不再走了。
points.egEn: The two princes simply lay down to rest and didn't move on any more.
points.zh: “干脆”，副词，表示做事直截了当、索性，常用在经过考虑后作出比较彻底的决定时。也可作形容词，表示说话做事爽快。
points.enx: “干脆” is an adverb meaning “simply; just; might as well”. It is used when someone makes a clear-cut decision after thinking it over. As an adjective it means “straightforward, frank”.
egs: （1）外面雨太大了，我们干脆明天再去吧。
（2）这件衣服太旧了，干脆扔了吧。

think: 国王为什么让两个儿子比赛？
为什么两个王子都不走了？
这个故事的关键办法是什么？

mc.q: 两个王子的马，（ ）。
options: 小王子的比大王子的马好
大王子的比小王子的马好

mc.q: 小王子要骑哥哥的马，是因为（ ）。
options: 他想让哥哥的马先到终点

mc.q: 国王让小王子做继承人，是因为他（ ）。

tip.title: 逆向思维
tip.zh: 逆向思维就是从相反的方向去思考问题。很多时候，人们习惯按照常规的方法想问题，可是遇到困难时，换一个角度，也许就能找到更好的办法。中国有一个家喻户晓的故事“司马光砸缸”：一个小朋友掉进了装满水的大缸里，别的孩子想把他从缸里拉出来，却怎么也拉不动。司马光没有想办法“让人离开水”，而是拿起石头把缸砸破，“让水离开人”，救出了小朋友。这就是逆向思维。
tip.en: Reverse thinking means thinking about a problem from the opposite direction. People usually think in the usual way, but when they meet a difficulty, looking from another angle may lead to a better solution. There is a story every Chinese person knows, “Sima Guang Smashes the Vat”: a child fell into a big vat full of water, and the other children tried to pull him out but couldn't. Instead of trying to “take the child away from the water”, Sima Guang picked up a stone and smashed the vat to “take the water away from the child”, and so saved him. That is reverse thinking.

lessons.title: 香港的大排档
lessons.en: Hong Kong's Dai Pai Dong (Street Food Stalls)
lessons.daodu: 如果你在晚上出来逛街，可能会看到路边摆出了很多桌子，人们在那里边吃边喝边聊，那就是大排档。
lessons.daoduEn: If you go out for a stroll in the evening, you may see lots of tables set out by the roadside, with people eating, drinking and chatting all at once. That is a dai pai dong.

paras.zh: 香港是一个多种文化汇集的地方，有很多东西都是外来的，但是大排档却不是。
paras.py: Xiānggǎng shì yí gè duō zhǒng wénhuà huìjí de dìfang, yǒu hěn duō dōngxi dōu shì wàilái de, dànshì dàpáidàng què bú shì.
paras.en: Hong Kong is a place where many cultures meet. Many things there came from outside, but the dai pai dong (open-air food stall) did not.

paras.zh: 所谓大排档，是指一种餐饮方式。店主在人行道边小巷中摆出几张桌子，客人就在这种露天或半露天的环境下吃饭。大排档里食物的种类很多，大都比较便宜。大排档一般从傍晚开始营业，直到深夜才结束，这是大排档的一大特色。
paras.py: Suǒwèi dàpáidàng, shì zhǐ yì zhǒng cānyǐn fāngshì. Diànzhǔ zài rénxíngdào biān xiǎoxiàng zhōng bǎichū jǐ zhāng zhuōzi, kèrén jiù zài zhè zhǒng lùtiān huò bàn lùtiān de huánjìng xià chīfàn. Dàpáidàng li shíwù de zhǒnglèi hěn duō, dà dōu bǐjiào piányi. Dàpáidàng yìbān cóng bàngwǎn kāishǐ yíngyè, zhídào shēnyè cái jiéshù, zhè shì dàpáidàng de yí dà tèsè.
paras.en: A dai pai dong is a way of eating out. The owner sets up a few tables beside the sidewalk or in a small lane, and customers eat outdoors or half outdoors. There are many kinds of food, and most of it is fairly cheap. Dai pai dong usually open in the evening and don't close until late at night - this is one of their main features.

paras.zh: 对于大排档的来历，大概很多经常吃大排档的人都不知道。其实，大排档在第二次世界大战后才出现。当时一些香港公务员在战争中受伤或死亡，政府为了帮助他们和他们的家人，就发给他们一种执照，允许他们在路边开小饭馆。由于食物好吃又便宜，所以这些小饭馆非常受欢迎。在广东话里，“档”是“小摊”的意思，又因为政府发的执照很大，所以大家就把这些在路边的小饭馆叫做“大牌档”。20世纪60年代是大排档的黄金时期，来吃饭的人很多，所以人们把“大牌档”改成了“大排档”，并一直用到现在。
paras.py: Duìyú dàpáidàng de láilì, dàgài hěn duō jīngcháng chī dàpáidàng de rén dōu bù zhīdào. Qíshí, dàpáidàng zài Dì-èr Cì Shìjiè Dàzhàn hòu cái chūxiàn. Dāngshí yìxiē Xiānggǎng gōngwùyuán zài zhànzhēng zhōng shòushāng huò sǐwáng, zhèngfǔ wèile bāngzhù tāmen hé tāmen de jiārén, jiù fā gěi tāmen yì zhǒng zhízhào, yǔnxǔ tāmen zài lù biān kāi xiǎo fànguǎn. Yóuyú shíwù hǎochī yòu piányi, suǒyǐ zhèxiē xiǎo fànguǎn fēicháng shòu huānyíng. Zài Guǎngdōnghuà li, “dàng” shì “xiǎotān” de yìsi, yòu yīnwèi zhèngfǔ fā de zhízhào hěn dà, suǒyǐ dàjiā jiù bǎ zhèxiē zài lù biān de xiǎo fànguǎn jiàozuò “dàpáidàng”. 20 shìjì 60 niándài shì dàpáidàng de huángjīn shíqī, lái chīfàn de rén hěn duō, suǒyǐ rénmen bǎ “dàpáidàng” gǎichéngle “dàpáidàng”, bìng yìzhí yòngdào xiànzài.
paras.en: Many people who often eat at dai pai dong probably don't know where they came from. In fact, they only appeared after World War II. At that time some Hong Kong civil servants had been injured or killed in the war. To help them and their families, the government gave them a kind of license that allowed them to open small restaurants by the roadside. Because the food was tasty and cheap, these little restaurants became very popular. In Cantonese, "dang" means "stall", and because the licenses (牌 pai, "sign/license") the government issued were large, people called these roadside restaurants "大牌档" - "big-license stalls". The 1960s were the golden age of dai pai dong; so many people came to eat that the name was changed to "大排档" (排 pai, "row" - stalls in rows), which is still used today. (Both are pronounced dàpáidàng.)

paras.zh: 到了20世纪80年代，政府认为大排档影响香港的交通和卫生，所以把大排档渐渐送进了饭店。但是它仍然能够吸引不少人，因为它改变的只是环境而不是味道。
paras.py: Dàole 20 shìjì 80 niándài, zhèngfǔ rènwéi dàpáidàng yǐngxiǎng Xiānggǎng de jiāotōng hé wèishēng, suǒyǐ bǎ dàpáidàng jiànjiàn sòngjìnle fàndiàn. Dànshì tā réngrán nénggòu xīyǐn bù shǎo rén, yīnwèi tā gǎibiàn de zhǐ shì huánjìng ér bú shì wèidao.
paras.en: By the 1980s, the government felt that dai pai dong were affecting Hong Kong's traffic and hygiene, so it gradually moved them into indoor restaurants. But they still attract many people, because only the setting has changed, not the taste.

points.name: 却
points.eg: 但是大排档却不是。
points.egEn: ...but the dai pai dong is not (one of the imported things).
points.zh: “却”，副词，表示转折，语气比“但是”轻，用在主语后面、动词前面，常和“但是、可是”一起用。
points.enx: “却” is an adverb showing contrast (“but; yet”). It is milder than 但是, comes after the subject and before the verb, and is often used together with 但是 or 可是.
egs: （1）他学汉语的时间不长，汉语却说得很好。
（2）天气很冷，他却只穿了一件衬衫。

points.name: 所谓
points.eg: 所谓大排档，是指一种餐饮方式。
points.egEn: The so-called dai pai dong refers to a style of eating out.
points.zh: “所谓”用来提出需要解释的词语，常用格式是“所谓A，是指/就是……”，后面对A进行说明。
points.enx: “所谓” (so-called; what is called) introduces a term that needs explaining, usually in the pattern “所谓A，是指/就是……”, followed by the explanation.
egs: （1）所谓“丝绸之路”，是指古代连接中国和西方的商路。
（2）所谓“好朋友”，就是在你有困难的时候帮助你的人。

think: 大排档最早是什么样的？
大排档是怎么产生的？
现在的大排档有什么变化？

tf.q: 大排档最早出现在香港。
大排档的食品一般都很贵。
晚上营业是大排档的一个特色。

mc.q: 大排档发展的黄金时期是（ ）。
下面的说法正确的是（ ）。
options: 大排档一般在室内营业
大排档常常在白天营业
大排档进入饭店以后，味道改变了

tip.title: 东方之珠——香港
tip.zh: 香港位于中国南部、珠江口的东边，由香港岛、九龙和新界三部分组成。1997年7月1日，香港回归中国，成为中华人民共和国的特别行政区。香港是重要的国际金融、贸易和航运中心，也是著名的旅游城市。这里东西方文化交融，高楼林立，夜景非常美丽，还有“购物天堂”和“美食天堂”的称号。因为它像一颗明珠一样闪闪发光，所以人们把香港叫做“东方之珠”。
tip.en: Hong Kong lies in southern China, on the east side of the Pearl River estuary, and is made up of three parts: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon and the New Territories. On 1 July 1997 Hong Kong returned to China and became a Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China. It is an important international centre of finance, trade and shipping, and a famous tourist city. Here Eastern and Western cultures blend, skyscrapers stand side by side and the night view is stunning; it is also known as a “shopping paradise” and a “food paradise”. Because it shines like a bright pearl, people call Hong Kong the “Pearl of the Orient”.

lessons.title: 一美元的汽车
lessons.daodu: 一美元买一辆豪华汽车，如果在报纸上看到这样的广告，你会相信吗？
lessons.daoduEn: A luxury car for one dollar—if you saw an ad like this in a newspaper, would you believe it?

paras.zh: 美国的一家报纸上登了这样一个广告：“一美元买一辆豪华汽车。”
paras.py: Měiguó de yì jiā bàozhǐ shang dēngle zhèyàng yí gè guǎnggào: “Yì měiyuán mǎi yí liàng háohuá qìchē.”
paras.en: An American newspaper ran this ad: "Buy a luxury car for one dollar."

paras.zh: 哈利看到广告，心想：今天不是四月一号啊！但他还是带着一美元去了。
paras.py: Hālì kàndào guǎnggào, xīn xiǎng: Jīntiān bú shì sì yuè yī hào a! Dàn tā háishi dàizhe yì měiyuán qù le.
paras.en: When Harry saw the ad, he thought: "Today isn't April 1st!" But he went anyway, taking one dollar with him.

paras.zh: 在一栋非常漂亮的房子前面，哈利敲开了门。
paras.py: Zài yí dòng fēicháng piàoliang de fángzi qiánmian, Hālì qiāokāile mén.
paras.en: In front of a very beautiful house, Harry knocked on the door.

paras.zh: 一位少妇为他打开门，问清楚后，少妇带哈利来到车库，指着一辆豪华汽车说：“就是它。”
paras.py: Yí wèi shàofù wèi tā dǎkāi mén, wèn qīngchu hòu, shàofù dài Hālì láidào chēkù, zhǐzhe yí liàng háohuá qìchē shuō: “Jiù shì tā.”
paras.en: A young woman opened the door. After asking what he had come for, she took Harry to the garage, pointed at a luxury car and said, "This is it."

paras.zh: 哈利脑子里闪过的第一个念头就是：“是坏车。”就问：“太太，我可以试试吗？”
paras.py: Hālì nǎozi li shǎnguo de dì-yī gè niàntou jiù shì: “Shì huài chē.” Jiù wèn: “Tàitai, wǒ kěyǐ shìshi ma?”
paras.en: The first thought that flashed through Harry's mind was: "It must be broken." So he asked, "Ma'am, may I try it?"

paras.zh: “当然可以！”于是哈利开着车转了一圈，一切正常。
paras.py: “Dāngrán kěyǐ!” Yúshì Hālì kāizhe chē zhuànle yì quān, yíqiè zhèngcháng.
paras.en: "Of course!" So Harry drove the car around the block. Everything was fine.

paras.zh: “这辆车不是偷来的吧？”哈利要求看一下发票，少妇拿给他看了。
paras.py: “Zhè liàng chē bú shì tōu lái de ba?” Hālì yāoqiú kàn yíxià fāpiào, shàofù ná gěi tā kàn le.
paras.en: "This car isn't stolen, is it?" Harry asked to see the receipt, and the woman showed it to him.

paras.zh: 一切都没问题后，哈利付了一美元。当他开车要离开的时候，心里仍然非常好奇。他问：“太太，您能告诉我这是为什么吗？”
paras.py: Yíqiè dōu méi wèntí hòu, Hālì fùle yì měiyuán. Dāng tā kāi chē yào líkāi de shíhou, xīn li réngrán fēicháng hàoqí. Tā wèn: “Tàitai, nín néng gàosu wǒ zhè shì wèishénme ma?”
paras.en: When everything checked out, Harry paid one dollar. As he was about to drive away, he was still very curious. He asked, "Ma'am, can you tell me why?"

paras.zh: 少妇叹了一口气：“唉，实话跟你说吧，我丈夫死了。他把一切都留给了我，只有这辆车，是属于他那个情妇的。但是，他把这辆车的拍卖权交给了我，拍卖的钱交给他的情妇。所以，我决定卖掉它，一美元就可以。”
paras.py: Shàofù tànle yì kǒu qì: “Āi, shíhuà gēn nǐ shuō ba, wǒ zhàngfu sǐ le. Tā bǎ yíqiè dōu liú gěile wǒ, zhǐyǒu zhè liàng chē, shì shǔyú tā nàge qíngfù de. Dànshì, tā bǎ zhè liàng chē de pāimàiquán jiāo gěile wǒ, pāimài de qián jiāo gěi tā de qíngfù. Suǒyǐ, wǒ juédìng màidiào tā, yì měiyuán jiù kěyǐ.”
paras.en: The woman sighed: "Well, to tell you the truth, my husband died. He left everything to me except this car, which belongs to his mistress. But he gave me the right to sell it, with the money going to his mistress. So I decided to sell it - for just one dollar."

paras.zh: 哈利恍然大悟，他开着车高高兴兴地回家了。路上，哈利碰到了他的朋友汤姆。汤姆好奇地问这辆车的来历。等哈利说完，汤姆一下子坐在了地上：“啊！一周前我就看到这个广告了！”
paras.py: Hālì huǎngrán dàwù, tā kāizhe chē gāogāoxìngxìng de huí jiā le. Lù shang, Hālì pèngdàole tā de péngyou Tāngmǔ. Tāngmǔ hàoqí de wèn zhè liàng chē de láilì. Děng Hālì shuōwán, Tāngmǔ yíxiàzi zuò zài le dì shang: “À! Yì zhōu qián wǒ jiù kàndào zhège guǎnggào le!”
paras.en: Suddenly Harry understood, and he drove home happily. On the way he ran into his friend Tom. Tom curiously asked where the car had come from. When Harry finished, Tom sank to the ground: "Oh no! I saw that ad a week ago!"

points.name: 闪过（一个）念头
points.en: an idea flashing through one’s mind
points.eg: 哈利脑子里闪过的第一个念头就是：“是坏车。”
points.egEn: The first thought that flashed through Harry's mind was: “It must be a broken car.”
points.zh: “念头”，名词，意思是心里的想法。“闪过一个念头”表示一个想法突然、很快地出现在脑子里。
points.enx: “念头” is a noun meaning “thought, idea”. “闪过一个念头” means “an idea suddenly flashes through one's mind”.
egs: （1）看到那张旅游广告，我脑子里闪过一个念头：放假去海南玩儿。
（2）他心里闪过一个念头：是不是自己走错路了？

points.name: 属于
points.eg: 只有这辆车，是属于他那个情妇的。
points.egEn: Only this car belonged to that mistress of his.
points.zh: “属于”，动词，表示归某一方所有，或者是某一类中的一个，后面跟名词或代词。
points.enx: “属于” means “to belong to”. It shows ownership or that something is part of a certain category, and is followed by a noun or pronoun.
egs: （1）这些书都属于学校图书馆，不能带回家。
（2）大熊猫属于国家保护动物。

think: 哈利看到广告时，为什么觉得奇怪？
哈利的朋友听了哈利的话后为什么心痛？

tf.q: “一美元买一辆汽车”是一个愚人节的玩笑。
那辆汽车有一点毛病，所以很便宜。
汽车的拍卖权不是这位少妇的。
哈利的朋友不相信这个广告是真的。

mc.q: 那辆豪华汽车少妇只卖一美元，是因为（ ）。
options: 她不想给那个情妇很多钱
她的丈夫让她卖一美元

mc.q: 这一美元最后应该给（ ）。
哈利的朋友坐在地上，是因为（ ）。
options: 他当初不相信这个广告，现在非常后悔
他没有看报纸，错过了机会

tip.title: 生活中充满奇迹
tip.zh: 生活中常常会发生一些让人意想不到的事情。有的人觉得这只是巧合，有的人却把它们叫做“奇迹”。其实，很多“奇迹”并不是从天上掉下来的，而是属于那些愿意相信、敢于尝试的人。就像课文里的哈利，他虽然也怀疑“一美元买豪华汽车”的广告，但还是带着一美元去看了看，结果真的得到了一辆好车；而他的朋友汤姆早就看到了广告，却因为不相信而错过了机会。所以，面对机会的时候，不妨多一点儿好奇心和勇气。
tip.en: Unexpected things often happen in life. Some people think they are just coincidences, while others call them “miracles”. In fact, many “miracles” don't fall from the sky; they belong to people who are willing to believe and dare to try. Take Harry in the text: although he too doubted the ad offering “a luxury car for one dollar”, he still went along with a dollar to have a look—and really got a fine car. His friend Tom had seen the ad long before, but missed the chance because he didn't believe it. So when an opportunity comes along, it is worth having a little more curiosity and courage.

lessons.title: 大导演，小故事
lessons.daodu: 很多成功人士常常因为工作忙而没有时间照顾家人，但大导演李安却不是这样。
lessons.daoduEn: Many successful people have no time to look after their families because they are busy with work, but the great director Ang Lee is not like that.

paras.zh: 在事业上，李安是国际著名的大导演，拍过很多精彩的电影，也得过很多大奖。在生活中，他是一位关心妻子儿女的好丈夫、好父亲。
paras.py: Zài shìyè shang, Lǐ Ān shì guójì zhùmíng de dà dǎoyǎn, pāiguo hěn duō jīngcǎi de diànyǐng, yě déguo hěn duō dàjiǎng. Zài shēnghuó zhōng, tā shì yí wèi guānxīn qīzi érnǚ de hǎo zhàngfu, hǎo fùqin.
paras.en: In his career, Ang Lee is a world-famous director who has made many wonderful films and won many major awards. In his private life, he is a good husband and father who cares about his wife and children.

paras.zh: 成功前，李安生活得很艰苦。他没有工作，全靠妻子在外面工作养家。当他的电影《喜宴》在柏林电影节上获得金熊奖后，朋友请他吃饭，为他庆祝。谁知道菜刚一上来，李安竟然大哭起来。朋友觉得很奇怪，问他怎么回事。原来，李安想起了在纽约家里的妻子和孩子，想起了全家人一起度过的苦日子。李安很希望在这个时候能跟他们一起庆祝。
paras.py: Chénggōng qián, Lǐ Ān shēnghuó de hěn jiānkǔ. Tā méiyǒu gōngzuò, quán kào qīzi zài wàimian gōngzuò yǎng jiā. Dāng tā de diànyǐng “Xǐyàn” zài Bólín Diànyǐngjié shang huòdé Jīnxióngjiǎng hòu, péngyou qǐng tā chīfàn, wèi tā qìngzhù. Shéi zhīdào cài gāng yí shànglai, Lǐ Ān jìngrán dà kū qǐlai. Péngyou juéde hěn qíguài, wèn tā zěnme huí shì. Yuánlái, Lǐ Ān xiǎngqǐle zài Niǔyuē jiā li de qīzi hé háizi, xiǎngqǐle quánjiārén yìqǐ dùguò de kǔ rìzi. Lǐ Ān hěn xīwàng zài zhège shíhou néng gēn tāmen yìqǐ qìngzhù.
paras.en: Before he became successful, Ang Lee lived a hard life. He had no job and relied entirely on his wife working to support the family. When his film The Wedding Banquet won the Golden Bear at the Berlin Film Festival, friends took him out to dinner to celebrate. As soon as the first dishes arrived, Ang Lee suddenly burst into tears. His friends found this strange and asked what was going on. It turned out he was thinking of his wife and children at home in New York, and of the hard days the whole family had been through together. He very much wished he could celebrate with them at that moment.

paras.zh: 即使是很有名以后，李安仍然抽空照顾妻子儿女。有一天，李安夫妇去市场买菜。路上有人认出了李安，忍不住对他妻子说：“你命真好，先生现在还有空儿陪你买菜！”没想到妻子却说：“不是他陪我，是我今天特意抽空陪他！”原来李安成为大导演后还一直坚持买菜做饭，不愿意让妻子太辛苦，难怪他们夫妻俩的感情这么好。
paras.py: Jíshǐ shì hěn yǒumíng yǐhòu, Lǐ Ān réngrán chōukòng zhàogù qīzi érnǚ. Yǒu yì tiān, Lǐ Ān fūfù qù shìchǎng mǎi cài. Lù shang yǒu rén rènchūle Lǐ Ān, rěnbuzhù duì tā qīzi shuō: “Nǐ mìng zhēn hǎo, xiānsheng xiànzài hái yǒu kòngr péi nǐ mǎi cài!” Méi xiǎngdào qīzi què shuō: “Bú shì tā péi wǒ, shì wǒ jīntiān tèyì chōukòng péi tā!” Yuánlái Lǐ Ān chéngwéi dà dǎoyǎn hòu hái yìzhí jiānchí mǎi cài zuòfàn, bú yuànyì ràng qīzi tài xīnkǔ, nánguài tāmen fūqī liǎ de gǎnqíng zhème hǎo.
paras.en: Even after becoming very famous, Ang Lee still made time to take care of his wife and children. One day, he and his wife went to the market to buy groceries. On the way, someone recognized him and couldn't help saying to his wife: "You're so lucky - your husband still has time to go grocery shopping with you!" Unexpectedly, his wife said: "He isn't keeping me company - I specially made time today to keep him company!" It turned out that even after becoming a great director, Ang Lee kept buying groceries and cooking, unwilling to let his wife work too hard. No wonder the couple are so close.

points.name: 原来
points.eg: 原来，李安想起了在纽约家里的妻子和孩子。
points.egEn: It turned out that Ang Lee had thought of his wife and children at home in New York.
points.zh: “原来”，副词，表示发现了以前不知道的真实情况，有恍然大悟的意思，常用在句首。
points.enx: “原来” is an adverb meaning “it turns out that; so that's why”. It shows that the speaker has found out the real situation he or she didn't know before, and it often starts a sentence.
egs: （1）我说怎么找不到他，原来他回国了。
（2）教室里怎么这么冷？原来窗户没关。

points.name: 难怪
points.eg: 难怪他们夫妻俩的感情这么好。
points.egEn: No wonder the couple get along so well.
points.zh: “难怪”，副词，表示明白了原因以后，对某种情况不再觉得奇怪，常和“原来”配合使用。
points.enx: “难怪” is an adverb meaning “no wonder”. Once the reason is understood, the situation no longer seems strange. It is often used together with 原来.
egs: （1）原来他在中国住过五年，难怪汉语说得这么好。
（2）外面下雪了，难怪这么冷。

think: 你喜欢看电影吗？你看过李安导演的电影吗？
为什么李安和妻子感情那么好？

tf.q: 李安是一位著名的电影导演。
成功以前，李安生活得很好。
因为《喜宴》获奖了，所以李安和朋友一起吃饭。

mc.q: 和朋友一起吃饭时，李安哭了，是因为（ ）。
options: 他想起他的妻子和孩子

mc.q: 有了名之后，李安仍然坚持去买菜，是因为他（ ）。

tip.title: 李安
tip.zh: 李安1954年出生于台湾，是享誉世界的华人导演。他年轻时到美国学习戏剧和电影，毕业后有好几年找不到拍电影的机会，生活很艰苦。20世纪90年代初，他拍摄了《推手》《喜宴》《饮食男女》，这三部电影被称为“父亲三部曲”。后来，他的《卧虎藏龙》获得了奥斯卡最佳外语片奖，《断背山》和《少年派的奇幻漂流》又让他两次获得奥斯卡最佳导演奖，他也是第一位获得这个奖的亚洲导演。
tip.en: Ang Lee, born in Taiwan in 1954, is a world-renowned Chinese director. As a young man he went to the United States to study theatre and film, and after graduating he could not get a chance to make a film for several years, so life was hard. In the early 1990s he made “Pushing Hands”, “The Wedding Banquet” and “Eat Drink Man Woman”, known as the “Father Knows Best” trilogy. Later, his “Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon” won the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film, and “Brokeback Mountain” and “Life of Pi” each won him the Oscar for Best Director, making him the first Asian director to win that award.

lessons.title: 中国“狗”和西方“狗”
lessons.daodu: 狗是生活中常见的动物，但是不同的文化对它的态度却很不一样。
lessons.daoduEn: Dogs are common animals in everyday life, but different cultures have very different attitudes towards them.

paras.zh: 狗是和人们生活联系很紧密的动物，但是中西方文化对狗的看法却有很大的差异。
paras.py: Gǒu shì hé rénmen shēnghuó liánxì hěn jǐnmì de dòngwù, dànshì Zhōng-Xīfāng wénhuà duì gǒu de kànfǎ què yǒu hěn dà de chāyì.
paras.en: Dogs are animals closely connected to people's lives, but Chinese and Western cultures see dogs very differently.

paras.zh: 虽然现在很多家庭都很喜欢狗，把狗当作宠物，但是在过去，中国人一般认为狗是看家的动物，不是人们的宠物。因此与狗有关的词语大多是贬义的，如“走狗”、“狗眼看人低”等。
paras.py: Suīrán xiànzài hěn duō jiātíng dōu hěn xǐhuan gǒu, bǎ gǒu dàngzuò chǒngwù, dànshì zài guòqù, Zhōngguórén yìbān rènwéi gǒu shì kānjiā de dòngwù, bú shì rénmen de chǒngwù. Yīncǐ yǔ gǒu yǒuguān de cíyǔ dàduō shì biǎnyì de, rú “zǒugǒu”, “gǒu yǎn kàn rén dī” děng.
paras.en: Although many families today love dogs and keep them as pets, in the past Chinese people generally saw dogs as animals for guarding the house, not as pets. So most Chinese words about dogs are negative, such as "zougou" ("running dog", a lackey) and "gou yan kan ren di" ("a dog's eyes look down on people", i.e. a snob).

paras.zh: 而在西方文化中，人们对狗有特别的感情，认为狗十分可爱，聪明和忠实。狗被视为人类最好的朋友，在主人家中的地位很高，有专门的狗屋、狗粮、各种狗玩具，有的人甚至把狗当成家庭成员。英语中还常常用“dog”（狗）指人，意思相当于“fellow”（朋友）。例如，“a lucky dog”（幸运儿），就带有喜爱的意思。英语中还有其他许多与狗有关的习语，也大多是褒义的，如“love me, love my dog”（爱屋及乌）。
paras.py: Ér zài xīfāng wénhuà zhōng, rénmen duì gǒu yǒu tèbié de gǎnqíng, rènwéi gǒu shífēn kě'ài, cōngming hé zhōngshí. Gǒu bèi shìwéi rénlèi zuì hǎo de péngyou, zài zhǔrén jiā zhōng de dìwèi hěn gāo, yǒu zhuānmén de gǒuwū, gǒuliáng, gè zhǒng gǒu wánjù, yǒu de rén shènzhì bǎ gǒu dàngchéng jiātíng chéngyuán. Yīngyǔ zhōng hái chángcháng yòng “dog” (gǒu) zhǐ rén, yìsi xiāngdāng yú “fellow” (péngyou). Lìrú, “a lucky dog” (xìngyùn'ér), jiù dàiyǒu xǐ'ài de yìsi. Yīngyǔ zhōng hái yǒu qítā xǔduō yǔ gǒu yǒuguān de xíyǔ, yě dàduō shì bāoyì de, rú “love me, love my dog” (ài wū jí wū).
paras.en: In Western culture, however, people have special feelings for dogs and think they are lovely, clever and loyal. Dogs are seen as humans' best friend and have a high status in the home, with their own doghouses, dog food and all kinds of dog toys; some people even treat their dog as a family member. In English, "dog" is often used for a person, meaning something like "fellow". For example, "a lucky dog" carries a sense of fondness. English has many other dog idioms, mostly positive, such as "love me, love my dog" (Chinese 爱屋及乌, "love the house and you love the crow on its roof").

paras.zh: 另外，一些与狗有关的汉语和英语习语，虽然看起来一样，但文化含义却完全不同。比如“老狗”和“old dog”，“老狗”是骂人的话，“old dog”却是指“年纪大、经验丰富的人”。
paras.py: Lìngwài, yìxiē yǔ gǒu yǒuguān de Hànyǔ hé Yīngyǔ xíyǔ, suīrán kàn qǐlai yíyàng, dàn wénhuà hányì què wánquán bù tóng. Bǐrú “lǎo gǒu” hé “old dog”, “lǎo gǒu” shì mà rén de huà, “old dog” què shì zhǐ “niánjì dà, jīngyàn fēngfù de rén”.
paras.en: Also, some Chinese and English dog expressions look the same but have completely different cultural meanings. For example, "lao gou" and "old dog": in Chinese "lao gou" is an insult, but "old dog" refers to "an older, experienced person".

points.name: 大多
points.eg: 与狗有关的词语大多是贬义的。
points.egEn: Most words related to dogs are derogatory.
points.zh: “大多”，副词，表示大部分、大多数，用在动词或形容词前面。
points.enx: “大多” is an adverb meaning “mostly; for the most part”. It is used before a verb or an adjective.
egs: （1）我们班的同学大多来自欧洲。
（2）这个城市的公园大多是免费的。

points.name: 相当于
points.eg: 意思相当于“fellow”（朋友）。
points.egEn: Its meaning is equivalent to “fellow”.
points.zh: “相当于”，动词，表示两者在数量、价值、意思或作用等方面差不多一样。
points.enx: “相当于” means “to be equivalent to; to be about the same as” in amount, value, meaning or function.
egs: （1）一公里相当于两里。
（2）他一个月的工资相当于我三个月的工资。

think: 你知道哪些关于狗的词语？
在你的国家，狗有什么文化含义？
在你的母语和汉语中，还有哪些动物有着不同的含义？

tf.q: 过去中国人常用狗来看家。
汉语里有很多和狗有关的词语带有贬义。
狗在西方国家很受欢迎。
英语中用狗指人时，表示不喜欢这个人。
汉语和英语中有关狗的词，看起来一样，意思也一样。

tip.title: 动物比喻
tip.zh: 汉语和英语都喜欢用动物来比喻人，可是同一种动物在两种语言里的形象有时很不一样。比如龙，在中国是吉祥和力量的象征，父母“望子成龙”，希望孩子将来有出息；而在西方传说中，龙常常是可怕的怪物。猫头鹰在英语里常常代表聪明，在中国民间却常被认为不吉利。说一个人力气大，汉语说“力大如牛”，英语常说“as strong as a horse”。学习语言时了解这些不同，既有意思，也能避免误会。
tip.en: Both Chinese and English like to use animals in figures of speech about people, but the same animal can have a very different image in the two languages. The dragon, for example, is a symbol of good fortune and power in China—parents “hope their son becomes a dragon”, i.e. succeeds in life—while in Western legends dragons are often fearsome monsters. In English the owl often stands for wisdom, but in Chinese folk belief it is usually considered unlucky. To say someone is very strong, Chinese says “as strong as an ox”, while English often says “as strong as a horse”. Knowing these differences when learning a language is interesting and helps avoid misunderstandings.

lessons.title: 男人下厨好处多
lessons.en: Why It's Good for Men to Cook
lessons.daodu: 你会做饭吗？在你家，是父亲做饭还是母亲做饭？
lessons.daoduEn: Can you cook? In your family, does your father or your mother do the cooking?

paras.zh: 中国家庭的传统是“男主外，女主内”。意思就是说，男人负责在外面工作，挣钱养家，女人负责在家洗衣做饭，照顾孩子。
paras.py: Zhōngguó jiātíng de chuántǒng shì “nán zhǔ wài, nǚ zhǔ nèi”. Yìsi jiù shì shuō, nánrén fùzé zài wàimian gōngzuò, zhèng qián yǎng jiā, nǚrén fùzé zài jiā xǐ yī zuòfàn, zhàogù háizi.
paras.en: The traditional Chinese family follows "men take charge outside, women take charge inside". That is, men work outside and earn money to support the family, while women stay home to wash, cook and look after the children.

paras.zh: 而在现代社会中，越来越多的女人也开始工作，她们已经没有足够的时间和精力一个人做家务。因此，不少男人开始帮妻子做一些家务。尤其是在中国南方，很多男人经常下厨，而且能烧一手好菜。他们认为那样可以充分享受家的感觉，不仅可以减轻妻子的负担，还能增进夫妻感情。
paras.py: Ér zài xiàndài shèhuì zhōng, yuè lái yuè duō de nǚrén yě kāishǐ gōngzuò, tāmen yǐjīng méiyǒu zúgòu de shíjiān hé jīnglì yí gè rén zuò jiāwù. Yīncǐ, bù shǎo nánrén kāishǐ bāng qīzi zuò yìxiē jiāwù. Yóuqí shì zài Zhōngguó nánfāng, hěn duō nánrén jīngcháng xiàchú, érqiě néng shāo yì shǒu hǎo cài. Tāmen rènwéi nàyàng kěyǐ chōngfèn xiǎngshòu jiā de gǎnjué, bùjǐn kěyǐ jiǎnqīng qīzi de fùdān, hái néng zēngjìn fūqī gǎnqíng.
paras.en: But in modern society, more and more women work too, and they no longer have enough time and energy to do all the housework alone. So many men have started helping their wives with housework. Especially in southern China, many men often cook, and cook very well. They feel this lets them fully enjoy the feeling of home; it not only lightens their wives' load but also brings the couple closer.

paras.zh: 另外，男人下厨还对身体健康有好处。最近的研究发现，做饭也是很好的运动。一般来说，人们工作时只运用左脑，但是做饭可以运用右脑，让人的反应更快，从而起到锻炼身体的作用。另外，做饭可以培养人的判断力。什么时候放油，什么时候放菜，这些都是很有讲究的。做饭还可以培养分析能力。面对一道不熟悉的菜，优秀的厨师一般看一看、尝几口就知道大概应该怎么做。做饭同时也是一门艺术。要做出既好看又好吃的美食，自然也少不了想象力。
paras.py: Lìngwài, nánrén xiàchú hái duì shēntǐ jiànkāng yǒu hǎochù. Zuìjìn de yánjiū fāxiàn, zuòfàn yě shì hěn hǎo de yùndòng. Yìbān lái shuō, rénmen gōngzuò shí zhǐ yùnyòng zuǒnǎo, dànshì zuòfàn kěyǐ yùnyòng yòunǎo, ràng rén de fǎnyìng gèng kuài, cóng'ér qǐdào duànliàn shēntǐ de zuòyòng. Lìngwài, zuòfàn kěyǐ péiyǎng rén de pànduànlì. Shénme shíhou fàng yóu, shénme shíhou fàng cài, zhèxiē dōu shì hěn yǒu jiǎngjiu de. Zuòfàn hái kěyǐ péiyǎng fēnxī nénglì. Miànduì yí dào bù shúxī de cài, yōuxiù de chúshī yìbān kàn yi kàn, cháng jǐ kǒu jiù zhīdào dàgài yīnggāi zěnme zuò. Zuòfàn tóngshí yě shì yì mén yìshù. Yào zuòchū jì hǎokàn yòu hǎochī de měishí, zìrán yě shǎobuliǎo xiǎngxiànglì.
paras.en: Cooking is also good for men's health. Recent research has found that cooking is good exercise. Generally, people use only the left brain at work, but cooking uses the right brain, making people react faster and so serving as a workout. Cooking also trains judgment: when to add the oil and when to add the vegetables all take know-how. It trains analytical skills too: faced with an unfamiliar dish, a good cook can usually tell roughly how to make it after a look and a few tastes. Cooking is also an art. Making food that both looks and tastes good naturally requires imagination.

points.name: 起到……作用
points.eg: 从而起到锻炼身体的作用。
points.egEn: ...and thus have the effect of exercising the body.
points.zh: “起到……作用”表示产生某种效果或影响，“作用”前常加“重要的、很大的”或“动词短语+的”等定语。
points.enx: “起到……作用” means “to play a role; to have the effect of”. Modifiers such as 重要的, 很大的 or “verb phrase + 的” often come before 作用.
egs: （1）多读课文对提高口语能起到很大的作用。
（2）老师的鼓励起到了重要的作用，他越来越喜欢学习了。

points.name: 从而
points.eg: 让人的反应更快，从而起到锻炼身体的作用。
points.egEn: ...making people react faster, and thus exercising the body.
points.zh: “从而”，连词，用在后一个分句的开头，表示由于前面的原因或方法，产生了后面的结果或目的，多用于书面语。
points.enx: “从而” is a conjunction meaning “thus; thereby”. It begins the second clause and shows a result or purpose brought about by what was said before. It is mostly used in written Chinese.
egs: （1）他每天坚持锻炼，从而让自己的身体越来越好。
（2）这个城市修了很多条地铁，从而解决了交通问题。

think: 在你的国家，男人和女人有没有家庭分工？
“做饭是很好的运动”，你同意吗？

tf.q: “男人工作挣钱，女人做家务”是中国以前的传统。
做饭可以锻炼人的大脑。
在中国，南方男人经常做饭，北方男人根本不做饭。
做饭很简单，不需要创造力。

tip.title: 妇女在中国的地位
tip.zh: 在中国古代，妇女的地位比较低，很多女孩子没有机会上学。1949年以后，中国妇女的社会地位发生了很大的变化。1950年颁布的《婚姻法》规定男女权利平等、婚姻自由。“妇女能顶半边天”这句话，说明了妇女在社会中的重要作用。现在，越来越多的女性接受了高等教育，在各行各业工作，有的还成为了科学家、企业家和领导人。在很多家庭里，夫妻共同挣钱、共同分担家务，已经成为普遍的现象。
tip.en: In ancient China women had a fairly low status, and many girls had no chance to go to school. After 1949, the social status of Chinese women changed greatly. The Marriage Law issued in 1950 laid down equal rights for men and women and freedom of marriage. The saying “Women hold up half the sky” shows the important role women play in society. Today more and more women receive higher education and work in every field; some have become scientists, entrepreneurs and leaders. In many families it is now common for husband and wife to earn money together and share the housework.

lessons.title: 年画
lessons.daodu: 春节的时候，你会在很多中国人的家门上看到一幅画，一种娃娃抱着鲤鱼的传统年画。
lessons.daoduEn: During the Spring Festival you will see a picture on the doors of many Chinese homes: a traditional New Year picture of a baby holding a carp.

paras.zh: 年画是中国画的一种。在不同的地方，年画的名称也很不相同，现在逐渐地简称为“年画”。根据传统风俗，中国人在农历的腊月二十五这一天要在窗上和墙上贴上各种年画，希望新一年的生活能更加美好。
paras.py: Niánhuà shì Zhōngguóhuà de yì zhǒng. Zài bù tóng de dìfang, niánhuà de míngchēng yě hěn bù xiāngtóng, xiànzài zhújiàn de jiǎnchēng wéi “niánhuà”. Gēnjù chuántǒng fēngsú, Zhōngguórén zài nónglì de làyuè èrshíwǔ zhè yì tiān yào zài chuāng shang hé qiáng shang tiēshang gè zhǒng niánhuà, xīwàng xīn yì nián de shēnghuó néng gèngjiā měihǎo.
paras.en: New Year pictures are a kind of Chinese painting. They have different names in different places, but are now generally just called "nianhua". By tradition, on the 25th day of the 12th lunar month, Chinese people put up all kinds of New Year pictures on their windows and walls, hoping for a better life in the new year.

paras.zh: 年画有很长的历史，它最早是古代的门神画。传说从前有一位皇帝生病时，梦里常听到奇怪的声音，所以睡不好觉。后来，他的两位将军每天晚上站在门口守卫，夜里果然平安无事了。皇帝认为两位将军太辛苦了，所以就让人把这两位将军的样子画在门上，称为“门神”。
paras.py: Niánhuà yǒu hěn cháng de lìshǐ, tā zuì zǎo shì gǔdài de ménshénhuà. Chuánshuō cóngqián yǒu yí wèi huángdì shēngbìng shí, mèng li cháng tīngdào qíguài de shēngyīn, suǒyǐ shuì bù hǎo jiào. Hòulái, tā de liǎng wèi jiāngjūn měi tiān wǎnshang zhàn zài ménkǒu shǒuwèi, yè li guǒrán píng'ān wú shì le. Huángdì rènwéi liǎng wèi jiāngjūn tài xīnkǔ le, suǒyǐ jiù ràng rén bǎ zhè liǎng wèi jiāngjūn de yàngzi huà zài mén shang, chēngwéi “ménshén”.
paras.en: New Year pictures have a long history; the earliest were the door-god pictures of ancient times. Legend says an emperor once fell ill and often heard strange noises in his dreams, so he couldn't sleep well. Then two of his generals stood guard at his door every night, and sure enough, the nights became peaceful. The emperor felt the two generals were working too hard, so he had their images painted on the doors and called them "door gods".

paras.zh: 后来，年画的内容也变得多种多样，各种美好的事物或者民间传说都可以作为主题。每到过春节的时候，差不多每家都会买几张年画。从大门到室内，贴满了各种象征吉祥富贵的年画，其中最流行的要算是抱着鲤鱼的胖娃娃了。年画对春节的热闹气氛也起了不少的作用呢。
paras.py: Hòulái, niánhuà de nèiróng yě biàn de duō zhǒng duō yàng, gè zhǒng měihǎo de shìwù huòzhě mínjiān chuánshuō dōu kěyǐ zuòwéi zhǔtí. Měi dào guò Chūnjié de shíhou, chàbuduō měi jiā dōu huì mǎi jǐ zhāng niánhuà. Cóng dàmén dào shìnèi, tiēmǎnle gè zhǒng xiàngzhēng jíxiáng fùguì de niánhuà, qízhōng zuì liúxíng de yào suàn shì bàozhe lǐyú de pàng wáwa le. Niánhuà duì Chūnjié de rènao qìfēn yě qǐle bù shǎo de zuòyòng ne.
paras.en: Later, New Year pictures came to show all sorts of things: any beautiful thing or folk legend could be a subject. Every Spring Festival, almost every family buys a few. From the front gate to the rooms inside, the house is covered with pictures symbolizing good luck and wealth; the most popular is probably a chubby baby holding a carp. New Year pictures add a lot to the lively atmosphere of the Spring Festival.

points.name: 果然
points.eg: 夜里果然平安无事了。
points.egEn: Sure enough, the nights were peaceful after that.
points.zh: “果然”，副词，表示事实和说的或想的一样，常用在动词或主语前。
points.enx: “果然” is an adverb meaning “as expected; sure enough”. It shows that what actually happened matches what was said or expected.
egs: （1）天气预报说今天有雨，下午果然下起了大雨。
（2）大家都说这家饭馆的菜好吃，我尝了一下，果然不错。

points.name: 算
points.eg: 其中最流行的要算是抱着鲤鱼的胖娃娃了。
points.egEn: The most popular of them must be the chubby baby holding a carp.
points.zh: “算”，动词，表示“被认为是、可以说是”，常说“要算”“算是”，用来指出在某一范围内最突出的。
points.enx: “算” is a verb meaning “to be regarded as; to count as”. In “要算” or “算是” it points out what stands out most within a group.
egs: （1）在我们班，汉语说得最好的要算大卫了。
（2）这里的冬天不算太冷。

think: 为什么春节期间要贴年画？
贴年画的风俗是怎么产生的？
现在的年画一般是什么内容的？

tf.q: 年画只贴在大门上。
现在最常见的年画是抱着鱼的胖娃娃。

mc.q: 按照传统，贴年画应该在（ ）。

options: 为了让屋里的鬼更安全
