tip.title: 杨柳青年画
tip.zh: 杨柳青年画产生于天津的杨柳青镇，是中国最有名的木版年画之一。它开始于明代，到了清代非常兴盛，与苏州的桃花坞年画一起被称为“南桃北柳”。杨柳青年画的制作方法很特别：先用木版印出线条，再由艺人用手工一笔一笔地画上颜色，所以叫“半印半画”。画上的娃娃、仕女和戏曲故事色彩鲜艳、形象生动，充满了喜庆的气氛。2006年，杨柳青木版年画被列入第一批国家级非物质文化遗产名录。
tip.en: Yangliuqing New Year pictures come from the town of Yangliuqing in Tianjin and are among China's most famous woodblock New Year prints. They began in the Ming Dynasty and flourished in the Qing Dynasty; together with the Taohuawu pictures of Suzhou they are known as “Taohuawu in the south, Yangliuqing in the north”. They are made in a special way: the outlines are first printed from woodblocks, then artists paint in the colours by hand, stroke by stroke—hence “half printed, half painted”. The babies, beautiful ladies and opera scenes in the pictures are bright and lively, full of festive cheer. In 2006, Yangliuqing woodblock New Year pictures were included in China's first list of national intangible cultural heritage.

lessons.title: 给妈妈的一封信
lessons.py: Gěi māma de yì fēng xìn
lessons.daodu: 你经常给爸爸妈妈写信吗？你有心里话会跟爸爸妈妈说吗？
lessons.daoduEn: Do you often write letters to your parents? Do you tell them what is really on your mind?

paras.zh: 亲爱的妈妈：
paras.py: Qīn'ài de māma:
paras.en: Dear Mum,

paras.zh: 您好！
paras.py: Nín hǎo!
paras.en: Hello!

paras.zh: 当您看到这封信时，一定觉得很奇怪，为什么生活在您身边的女儿还要给您写信呢？我想，写信更便于和您讲我的心里话。
paras.py: Dāng nín kàndào zhè fēng xìn shí, yídìng juéde hěn qíguài, wèishénme shēnghuó zài nín shēnbiān de nǚ'ér hái yào gěi nín xiě xìn ne? Wǒ xiǎng, xiě xìn gèng biànyú hé nín jiǎng wǒ de xīnlǐhuà.
paras.en: When you see this letter, you'll surely think it strange: why would the daughter who lives right beside you write you a letter? I think a letter makes it easier to tell you what's really in my heart.

paras.zh: 妈妈，您为了让我一心一意地学习，什么都不让我做。您总是说：“你的任务只有一个——学习。”参加课外活动？这些话多心烦吗？
paras.py: Māma, nín wèile ràng wǒ yìxīn-yíyì de xuéxí, shénme dōu bú ràng wǒ zuò. Nín zǒngshì shuō: “Nǐ de rènwu zhǐyǒu yí gè —— xuéxí.” Cānjiā kèwài huódòng? Zhèxiē huà duō xīnfán ma?
paras.en: Mum, so that I can concentrate on studying, you don't let me do anything else. You always say: "You have only one task - studying." Take part in after-school activities? Aren't these words upsetting?

paras.zh: 记得有一个星期天，您从市场买回来很多菜。我放下书本，高高兴兴地到厨房打算帮您做一些家务。可是，您却说：“放下吧！去复习功课，下次考好一些就行了。”我知道，您是责任很重的母亲，这没有错。我扔下菜，跑回自己的房间，伤心地哭了。妈妈，您还记得吗？有一次学校组织我们打扫操场，这对我来说并不难。可是，为了一个“爱”我，让我在家学习，请假替我去劳动。您知道我的同学们怎么说我吗？您这样每天只让我“读书，读书”，对我的成长有什么好处呢？
paras.py: Jìde yǒu yí gè xīngqītiān, nín cóng shìchǎng mǎi huílai hěn duō cài. Wǒ fàngxia shūběn, gāogāoxìngxìng de dào chúfáng dǎsuan bāng nín zuò yìxiē jiāwù. Kěshì, nín què shuō: “Fàngxia ba! Qù fùxí gōngkè, xià cì kǎo hǎo yìxiē jiù xíng le.” Wǒ zhīdào, nín shì zérèn hěn zhòng de mǔqin, zhè méiyǒu cuò. Wǒ rēngxia cài, pǎo huí zìjǐ de fángjiān, shāngxīn de kū le. Māma, nín hái jìde ma? Yǒu yí cì xuéxiào zǔzhī wǒmen dǎsǎo cāochǎng, zhè duì wǒ lái shuō bìng bù nán. Kěshì, wèile yí gè “ài” wǒ, ràng wǒ zài jiā xuéxí, qǐngjià tì wǒ qù láodòng. Nín zhīdào wǒ de tóngxuémen zěnme shuō wǒ ma? Nín zhèyàng měi tiān zhǐ ràng wǒ “dúshū, dúshū”, duì wǒ de chéngzhǎng yǒu shénme hǎochù ne?
paras.en: I remember one Sunday you came back from the market with lots of vegetables. I put down my books and happily went to the kitchen to help with the housework. But you said: "Put them down! Go and review your lessons - just do a bit better on the next test." I know you're a mother with a strong sense of responsibility, and that isn't wrong. I dropped the vegetables, ran back to my room and cried. Mum, do you still remember? Once the school organized us to clean the sports field, which wasn't hard for me at all. But out of "love" for me, you made me stay home and study, and asked for leave so you could do the work in my place. Do you know what my classmates said about me? What good does it do my growing up for you to make me just "study, study" every day?

paras.zh: 妈妈，我知道您非常爱我，但我真的不需要过度的“关照”，因为总有一天，我要一个人面对生活中的困难。请您理解我！
paras.py: Māma, wǒ zhīdào nín fēicháng ài wǒ, dàn wǒ zhēn de bù xūyào guòdù de “guānzhào”, yīnwèi zǒng yǒu yì tiān, wǒ yào yí gè rén miànduì shēnghuó zhōng de kùnnan. Qǐng nín lǐjiě wǒ!
paras.en: Mum, I know you love me very much, but I really don't need so much "looking after", because one day I'll have to face life's difficulties on my own. Please understand me!

paras.zh: 您的女儿：月月
paras.py: Nín de nǚ'ér: Yuèyue
paras.en: Your daughter, Yueyue

paras.zh: 六月三日　夜
paras.py: Liù yuè sān rì yè
paras.en: Night of June 3rd

points.name: 便于
points.eg: 我想，写信更便于和您讲我的心里话。
points.egEn: I think writing a letter makes it easier to tell you what is on my mind.
points.zh: “便于”，动词，表示比较容易做某事、方便做某事，后面跟动词或动词短语，多用于书面语。
points.enx: “便于” means “to be convenient for; to make it easy to”. It is followed by a verb or verb phrase and is mostly used in written Chinese.
egs: （1）为了便于联系，请留下你的电话号码。
（2）这种自行车很轻，便于携带。

points.name: 记得
points.eg: 妈妈，您还记得吗？
points.egEn: Mum, do you still remember?
points.zh: “记得”，动词，表示没有忘记，还能想起过去的人或事，否定形式是“不记得”。
points.enx: “记得” means “to remember”—to still be able to recall a past person or event. Its negative form is “不记得”.
egs: （1）我还记得第一次来中国时的样子。
（2）你还记得那家饭馆叫什么名字吗？

points.name: 总
points.eg: 因为总有一天，我要一个人面对生活中的困难。
points.egEn: Because sooner or later, I will have to face life's difficulties on my own.
points.zh: “总”，副词，在“总有一天”里表示“终究、早晚”，强调某种情况一定会发生。
points.enx: “总” is an adverb. In “总有一天” (some day, sooner or later) it means “eventually; after all”, stressing that something is sure to happen.
egs: （1）只要坚持努力，你总会成功的。
（2）别着急，问题总会解决的。

think: 女儿为什么要给妈妈写信？
你现在更喜欢写信还是发电子邮件？
女儿希望妈妈怎么做？

tf.q: “我”不好意思和妈妈面对面说这个问题，所以写信。
“我”很理解妈妈的安排，所以没有生气。
妈妈不让“我”参加学校的活动，是为了让“我”有更多的时间学习。
“我”觉得妈妈这样关心我，对“我”没有好处。

tip.title: 中国的“小皇帝”
tip.zh: 20世纪70年代末起，中国开始实行计划生育政策，很多城市家庭只有一个孩子。在这样的家庭里，常常是爷爷奶奶、姥姥姥爷和爸爸妈妈六个大人围着一个孩子转，孩子就像家里的“小皇帝”“小公主”。有的父母对孩子过度关心，什么事情都替孩子做，结果孩子虽然学习成绩不错，独立生活的能力却比较差，也不太会关心别人。现在，越来越多的父母认识到，让孩子自己做事、学会承担责任，才是真正的爱。
tip.en: From the late 1970s China began to carry out its family planning policy, and many urban families had only one child. In such families, six adults—two pairs of grandparents and the parents—often revolved around a single child, who became the family's “little emperor” or “little princess”. Some parents cared for their child too much and did everything for him or her; as a result, although the child might do well at school, he or she was poor at living independently and not very good at caring for others. Today more and more parents realize that letting children do things for themselves and learn to take responsibility is true love.

lessons.title: 说说三里屯
lessons.daodu: 如果你到过北京，我想你一定听说过三里屯吧？那么三里屯是个什么样的地方呢？
lessons.daoduEn: If you have been to Beijing, you must have heard of Sanlitun. So what kind of place is it?

paras.zh: 说到北京的三里屯，无论是留学生还是在北京工作的外国人，都没有人不知道。这个因酒吧而闻名的地方，现在已经成为外国人休闲娱乐的重要场所了。
paras.py: Shuōdào Běijīng de Sānlǐtún, wúlùn shì liúxuéshēng háishi zài Běijīng gōngzuò de wàiguórén, dōu méiyǒu rén bù zhīdào. Zhège yīn jiǔbā ér wénmíng de dìfang, xiànzài yǐjīng chéngwéi wàiguórén xiūxián yúlè de zhòngyào chǎngsuǒ le.
paras.en: When it comes to Beijing's Sanlitun, there's no foreign student or foreigner working in Beijing who hasn't heard of it. Famous for its bars, it has become an important place for foreigners to relax and have fun.

paras.zh: 三里屯位于朝阳区东部，因离城三里而得名。1962年这个地方开始建大使馆，20世纪60—70年代建成外交公寓群。三里屯逐渐发展成为外交人员居住、购物和进行外事活动的重要社区。现在的三里屯附近有包括加拿大、澳大利亚、法国、比利时、德国等在内的79个国家的使馆。
paras.py: Sānlǐtún wèiyú Cháoyáng Qū dōngbù, yīn lí chéng sān lǐ ér démíng. 1962 nián zhège dìfang kāishǐ jiàn dàshǐguǎn, 20 shìjì 60—70 niándài jiànchéng wàijiāo gōngyùqún. Sānlǐtún zhújiàn fāzhǎn chéngwéi wàijiāo rényuán jūzhù, gòuwù hé jìnxíng wàishì huódòng de zhòngyào shèqū. Xiànzài de Sānlǐtún fùjìn yǒu bāokuò Jiānádà, Àodàlìyà, Fǎguó, Bǐlìshí, Déguó děng zàinèi de 79 gè guójiā de shǐguǎn.
paras.en: Sanlitun is in the east of Chaoyang District. It got its name because it is three li (1.5 km) from the old city. Embassies began to be built here in 1962, and diplomatic apartment complexes were completed in the 1960s and 70s. Sanlitun gradually became an important community where diplomats live, shop and carry out foreign affairs. Today there are embassies of 79 countries near Sanlitun, including Canada, Australia, France, Belgium and Germany.

paras.zh: 1995年，两个从日本留学回来的年轻人在这里建起了第一家酒吧。经过十多年的发展，目前三里屯周围三千米的地区已经有几十家不同风格、不同特色的酒吧。在这里你可以尽情地选择自己喜爱的风格——浪漫的、热情的……
paras.py: 1995 nián, liǎng gè cóng Rìběn liúxué huílai de niánqīngrén zài zhèlǐ jiànqǐle dì-yī jiā jiǔbā. Jīngguò shí duō nián de fāzhǎn, mùqián Sānlǐtún zhōuwéi sān qiānmǐ de dìqū yǐjīng yǒu jǐ shí jiā bù tóng fēnggé, bù tóng tèsè de jiǔbā. Zài zhèlǐ nǐ kěyǐ jìnqíng de xuǎnzé zìjǐ xǐ'ài de fēnggé —— làngmàn de, rèqíng de...
paras.en: In 1995, two young people who had come back from studying in Japan opened the first bar here. After more than ten years, there are now dozens of bars of different styles and character within three kilometers of Sanlitun. Here you can freely choose whatever style you like - romantic, lively...

paras.zh: 三里屯是酒吧街，但又不仅仅是酒吧街，还是音乐街。到了晚上，酒吧里有很多乐队为人们激情地歌唱。很多著名的歌手也常常来三里屯演出。此外，三里屯还是一条美食街、服装街。现在的三里屯是各种人、各种文化、各种生活态度汇集的地方。人们在这里寻找着、享受着属于自己的那份满足感。
paras.py: Sānlǐtún shì jiǔbājiē, dàn yòu bù jǐnjǐn shì jiǔbājiē, hái shì yīnyuèjiē. Dàole wǎnshang, jiǔbā li yǒu hěn duō yuèduì wèi rénmen jīqíng de gēchàng. Hěn duō zhùmíng de gēshǒu yě chángcháng lái Sānlǐtún yǎnchū. Cǐwài, Sānlǐtún hái shì yì tiáo měishíjiē, fúzhuāngjiē. Xiànzài de Sānlǐtún shì gè zhǒng rén, gè zhǒng wénhuà, gè zhǒng shēnghuó tàidu huìjí de dìfang. Rénmen zài zhèlǐ xúnzhǎozhe, xiǎngshòuzhe shǔyú zìjǐ de nà fèn mǎnzúgǎn.
paras.en: Sanlitun is a bar street, but not only that - it's also a music street. At night, many bands sing passionately in the bars, and many famous singers often perform here. Sanlitun is also a street of good food and clothing. Today it is a place where all kinds of people, cultures and attitudes to life come together. Here people search for and enjoy their own kind of satisfaction.

points.name: 是……还是……
points.eg: 无论是留学生还是在北京工作的外国人，都没有人不知道。
points.egEn: Whether they are international students or foreigners working in Beijing, there is no one who doesn't know it.
points.zh: “无论是A还是B，都……”表示在任何条件下结果都一样，“是……还是……”列出两种（或几种）情况，后面常用“都”呼应。
points.enx: “无论是A还是B，都……” means “whether A or B, …”. 是……还是…… lists two (or more) possibilities, and the result is the same in every case; 都 usually follows.
egs: （1）无论是大人还是孩子，都喜欢看这个节目。
（2）不管是刮风还是下雨，他每天都去跑步。

points.name: 因……而……
points.eg: 这个因酒吧而闻名的地方，现在已经成为外国人休闲娱乐的重要场所了。
points.egEn: This place, famous for its bars, has now become an important spot for foreigners' leisure and entertainment.
points.zh: “因……而……”表示因果关系，“因”后面是原因，“而”后面是结果，多用于书面语。
points.enx: “因……而……” expresses cause and effect: the cause follows 因 and the result follows 而. It is used mostly in written Chinese.
egs: （1）杭州因西湖而闻名。
（2）这场比赛因天气不好而推迟了。

think: 三里屯为什么会成为酒吧街？
三里屯的酒吧有什么特色？
三里屯仅仅是一条酒吧街吗？

tf.q: 因为这个地方离城区三里，所以叫“三里屯”。
很多外国人在三里屯附近工作和生活。
三里屯酒吧街里常常有音乐表演。
现在的三里屯，不只有酒吧，还有音乐、美食、服装汇集的地方。

mc.q: 三里屯是从（ ）开始有酒吧的。
下面不是三里屯特点的是（ ）。

tip.title: 中国人的夜生活
tip.zh: 过去，中国人的生活习惯是“日出而作，日落而息”，晚上很少出去活动。随着经济的发展和城市生活的变化，中国人的夜生活越来越丰富。在大城市里，人们下班后可以去逛夜市、吃夜宵，也可以去酒吧、唱卡拉OK、看电影或者看演出，很多商场和饭店一直营业到深夜。年轻人喜欢晚上和朋友聚会，一些中老年人则喜欢在广场上跳舞、散步。丰富的夜生活也成为了城市活力的一种表现。
tip.en: In the past, Chinese people lived by the rule “work at sunrise, rest at sunset” and seldom went out in the evening. With economic development and changes in city life, Chinese night life has become richer and richer. In big cities, after work people can stroll around night markets and have late-night snacks, or go to bars, sing karaoke, see a film or watch a show, and many shopping centres and restaurants stay open until late at night. Young people like to get together with friends in the evening, while many middle-aged and older people like to dance or take a walk in public squares. A lively night life has become one sign of a city's vitality.

lessons.title: 十二生肖为什么没有猫？
lessons.en: Why Is There No Cat in the Chinese Zodiac?
lessons.daodu: 中国的十二生肖有十二种动物，都有哪些动物呢？
lessons.daoduEn: The Chinese zodiac has twelve animals. Which animals are they?

paras.zh: 中国的十二生肖是：鼠、牛、虎、兔、龙、蛇、马、羊、猴、鸡、狗、猪。你知道为什么有老鼠却没有猫吗？这里有个故事。
paras.py: Zhōngguó de shí'èr shēngxiào shì: shǔ, niú, hǔ, tù, lóng, shé, mǎ, yáng, hóu, jī, gǒu, zhū. Nǐ zhīdào wèishénme yǒu lǎoshǔ què méiyǒu māo ma? Zhèlǐ yǒu gè gùshi.
paras.en: The twelve Chinese zodiac animals are: rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, goat, monkey, rooster, dog and pig. Do you know why there's a rat but no cat? Here's a story.

paras.zh: 很早以前，人们要选十二种动物作为人的生肖，每年一种动物。可是动物太多了，怎么办呢？大家商量后选了个日子，让动物们在这一天来报名，最先报名的十二种动物就是十二生肖。
paras.py: Hěn zǎo yǐqián, rénmen yào xuǎn shí'èr zhǒng dòngwù zuòwéi rén de shēngxiào, měi nián yì zhǒng dòngwù. Kěshì dòngwù tài duō le, zěnme bàn ne? Dàjiā shāngliang hòu xuǎnle gè rìzi, ràng dòngwùmen zài zhè yì tiān lái bàomíng, zuì xiān bàomíng de shí'èr zhǒng dòngwù jiù shì shí'èr shēngxiào.
paras.en: Long ago, people wanted to choose twelve animals as zodiac signs, one animal for each year. But there were too many animals - what to do? After talking it over, they picked a day for the animals to come and sign up; the first twelve to sign up would be the twelve zodiac animals.

paras.zh: 猫和老鼠是邻居，又是好朋友。它们都想去报名。猫说：“咱们得早点儿起床去报名，可是我爱睡懒觉，怎么办呢？”老鼠说：“没关系，没关系。我一醒就去叫你，咱们一块儿去。”
paras.py: Māo hé lǎoshǔ shì línjū, yòu shì hǎo péngyou. Tāmen dōu xiǎng qù bàomíng. Māo shuō: “Zánmen děi zǎo diǎnr qǐchuáng qù bàomíng, kěshì wǒ ài shuì lǎnjiào, zěnme bàn ne?” Lǎoshǔ shuō: “Méi guānxi, méi guānxi. Wǒ yì xǐng jiù qù jiào nǐ, zánmen yíkuàir qù.”
paras.en: The cat and the rat were neighbors and good friends. Both wanted to sign up. The cat said: "We have to get up early to sign up, but I love sleeping in. What should I do?" The rat said: "No problem, no problem. I'll come and wake you as soon as I'm up, and we'll go together."

paras.zh: 猫听了很高兴，说：“你真是我的好朋友，谢谢你了。”
paras.py: Māo tīngle hěn gāoxìng, shuō: “Nǐ zhēn shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou, xièxie nǐ le.”
paras.en: The cat was very happy to hear this and said: "You really are my good friend. Thank you."

paras.zh: 到了报名的那天早晨，老鼠很早就醒了。可是它光想着自己的事，忘了好朋友猫，就自己去报名了。结果，老鼠被选上了，而猫因为起床太晚了，所以没有被选上。猫因此很生气。从此以后，猫见了老鼠就要吃它。
paras.py: Dàole bàomíng de nà tiān zǎochen, lǎoshǔ hěn zǎo jiù xǐng le. Kěshì tā guāng xiǎngzhe zìjǐ de shì, wàngle hǎo péngyou māo, jiù zìjǐ qù bàomíng le. Jiéguǒ, lǎoshǔ bèi xuǎnshang le, ér māo yīnwèi qǐchuáng tài wǎn le, suǒyǐ méiyǒu bèi xuǎnshang. Māo yīncǐ hěn shēngqì. Cóngcǐ yǐhòu, māo jiànle lǎoshǔ jiù yào chī tā.
paras.en: On the morning of sign-up day, the rat woke up very early. But it thought only of itself, forgot its good friend the cat, and went to sign up alone. As a result, the rat was chosen, but the cat got up too late and wasn't. The cat was very angry. Ever since, whenever a cat sees a rat, it wants to eat it.

paras.zh: 其实这只是个故事，并不是真的。十二生肖里有老鼠却没有猫，是因为猫是从国外传到中国的。中国出现“十二生肖”这个词的时候，还没有“猫”这个词呢。
paras.py: Qíshí zhè zhǐ shì gè gùshi, bìng bú shì zhēn de. Shí'èr shēngxiào li yǒu lǎoshǔ què méiyǒu māo, shì yīnwèi māo shì cóng guówài chuándào Zhōngguó de. Zhōngguó chūxiàn “shí'èr shēngxiào” zhège cí de shíhou, hái méiyǒu “māo” zhège cí ne.
paras.en: Actually, this is only a story, not true. The real reason there's a rat but no cat among the twelve zodiac animals is that cats came to China from abroad. When the word "twelve zodiac animals" appeared in China, there was no word for "cat" yet.

points.name: 得
points.eg: 咱们得早点儿起床去报名。
points.egEn: We need to get up early to sign up.
points.zh: “得（děi）”，助动词，表示情理上或事实上的需要，相当于“需要、应该”，多用于口语，否定用“不用”。
points.enx: “得” (pronounced děi) is an auxiliary verb meaning “need to; have to; must”. It is colloquial, and its negative form is “不用”.
egs: （1）时间不早了，我得回家了。
（2）这件事你得先跟父母商量一下。

points.name: 光
points.eg: 可是它光想着自己的事，忘了好朋友猫。
points.egEn: But it was only thinking about its own business and forgot its good friend the cat.
points.zh: “光”，副词，意思是“只、仅仅”，表示范围，用在动词或名词前。
points.enx: “光” is an adverb meaning “only; just”. It limits the scope and is used before a verb or a noun.
egs: （1）你别光看书，也要多出去运动运动。
（2）光我们班就有十几个人报名参加比赛。

think: 十二生肖里为什么有老鼠却没有猫？
猫为什么见了老鼠就要吃它？

tf.q: 鼠、鸡、鱼都是生肖中的动物。
因为猫容易忘事，所以它让老鼠第二天去叫它。
老鼠没有去叫猫，是因为它不想让猫成为生肖。
“猫”这个词是在十二生肖产生以后出现的。

tip.title: 本命年
tip.zh: 十二生肖每十二年循环一次，每个人都有一个属于自己的生肖。比如2008年是鼠年，这一年出生的人属鼠，以后每到鼠年，就是他的“本命年”。所以，人们在十二岁、二十四岁、三十六岁……的时候都会遇到本命年。按照中国的传统说法，本命年的运气可能不太好，所以很多人在本命年会穿红袜子、系红腰带、戴红绳，希望红色能带来好运，帮助自己平平安安地度过这一年。
tip.en: The twelve zodiac animals repeat in a twelve-year cycle, and everyone has a zodiac animal of his or her own. For example, 2008 was the Year of the Rat, so people born that year are Rats, and every later Year of the Rat is their “benming nian” (birth-sign year). People therefore meet their birth-sign year at the ages of 12, 24, 36 and so on. According to Chinese tradition, one's luck may not be so good in one's birth-sign year, so many people wear red socks, a red belt or a red string that year, hoping the colour red will bring good luck and help them get through the year safely.

lessons.title: 难忘的愚人节
lessons.daodu: 你喜欢和朋友开玩笑吗？有时候，和别人开玩笑可能最后却捉弄了自己。
lessons.daoduEn: Do you like playing jokes on your friends? Sometimes, playing a joke on others may end up making a fool of yourself.

paras.zh: 不知从什么时候开始，中国的大学校园里也开始流行起一个外国人的节日——“愚人节”了。每年的四月一日，校园里到处都在“说谎”，每个人都享受着捉弄别人的快乐。
paras.py: Bù zhī cóng shénme shíhou kāishǐ, Zhōngguó de dàxué xiàoyuán li yě kāishǐ liúxíng qǐ yí gè wàiguórén de jiérì —— “Yúrénjié” le. Měi nián de sì yuè yī rì, xiàoyuán li dàochù dōu zài “shuōhuǎng”, měi gè rén dōu xiǎngshòuzhe zhuōnòng biérén de kuàilè.
paras.en: Nobody knows exactly when it started, but a foreign holiday - April Fool's Day - has become popular on Chinese university campuses too. Every April 1st, people all over campus are "telling lies", and everyone enjoys the fun of playing tricks on others.

paras.zh: 下面是最让我难忘的一个愚人节。
paras.py: Xiàmian shì zuì ràng wǒ nánwàng de yí gè Yúrénjié.
paras.en: Here is the April Fool's Day I'll never forget.

paras.zh: 那时，我是我们班的班长。那天早上，我一进教室，就郑重地宣布：“今天下午我们有英语考试，大家要好好准备！”“真的呀？”“老师没有告诉过我们呀！”同学们问。“这你们还不懂吗？老师是想知道你们平时学习是不是很努力，就想做一次临时测验，她当然不会告诉你们了。”教室里立刻安静下来，紧接着，传来一阵阵朗读英语的声音。同学们有的在背课文，有的在记语法，有的在写生词。看到他们又紧张又认真的样子，我真想笑。
paras.py: Nà shí, wǒ shì wǒmen bān de bānzhǎng. Nà tiān zǎoshang, wǒ yí jìn jiàoshì, jiù zhèngzhòng de xuānbù: “Jīntiān xiàwǔ wǒmen yǒu Yīngyǔ kǎoshì, dàjiā yào hǎohāo zhǔnbèi!” “Zhēn de ya?” “Lǎoshī méiyǒu gàosuguo wǒmen ya!” Tóngxuémen wèn. “Zhè nǐmen hái bù dǒng ma? Lǎoshī shì xiǎng zhīdào nǐmen píngshí xuéxí shì bu shì hěn nǔlì, jiù xiǎng zuò yí cì línshí cèyàn, tā dāngrán bú huì gàosu nǐmen le.” Jiàoshì li lìkè ānjìng xiàlai, jǐn jiēzhe, chuánlái yí zhènzhèn lǎngdú Yīngyǔ de shēngyīn. Tóngxuémen yǒu de zài bèi kèwén, yǒu de zài jì yǔfǎ, yǒu de zài xiě shēngcí. Kàndào tāmen yòu jǐnzhāng yòu rènzhēn de yàngzi, wǒ zhēn xiǎng xiào.
paras.en: At that time I was our class monitor. That morning, as soon as I walked into the classroom, I solemnly announced: "We have an English test this afternoon. Everyone get ready!" "Really?" "The teacher never told us!" my classmates said. "Don't you get it? The teacher wants to know whether you study hard every day, so she wants to give a surprise quiz. Of course she won't tell you." The classroom went quiet at once, and then came the sound of people reading English aloud. Some were memorizing texts, some were going over grammar, some were writing new words. Seeing how nervous and serious they were, I really wanted to laugh.

paras.zh: 下午上英语课了，英语老师微笑着走进教室。让我没想到的是，老师竟然真的对我们说：“同学们，今天我们做一次临时测验，老师想了解一下你们平时的学习情况。请大家准备一下，三分钟以后，我们开始考试。”
paras.py: Xiàwǔ shàng Yīngyǔkè le, Yīngyǔ lǎoshī wēixiàozhe zǒujìn jiàoshì. Ràng wǒ méi xiǎngdào de shì, lǎoshī jìngrán zhēn de duì wǒmen shuō: “Tóngxuémen, jīntiān wǒmen zuò yí cì línshí cèyàn, lǎoshī xiǎng liǎojiě yíxià nǐmen píngshí de xuéxí qíngkuàng. Qǐng dàjiā zhǔnbèi yíxià, sān fēnzhōng yǐhòu, wǒmen kāishǐ kǎoshì.”
paras.en: In the afternoon English class, the English teacher walked in smiling. To my surprise, she actually said to us: "Class, today we'll have a surprise quiz. I'd like to see how you've been doing in your everyday studies. Please get ready - we'll start in three minutes."

paras.zh: 同学们都向我投来感谢的目光，然后就开始准备考试了。
paras.py: Tóngxuémen dōu xiàng wǒ tóulái gǎnxiè de mùguāng, ránhòu jiù kāishǐ zhǔnbèi kǎoshì le.
paras.en: My classmates all gave me grateful looks and then started getting ready for the test.

paras.zh: 我呢，好像突然被人泼了一盆冷水，傻了。
paras.py: Wǒ ne, hǎoxiàng tūrán bèi rén pōle yì pén lěngshuǐ, shǎ le.
paras.en: As for me, I felt as if someone had suddenly poured a bucket of cold water over me. I was stunned.

points.name: 形容词+下来
points.eg: 教室里立刻安静下来。
points.egEn: The classroom immediately went quiet.
points.zh: “形容词+下来”表示状态开始出现并继续发展，多用于由动到静、由强到弱的变化，如“安静下来”“冷静下来”“暗下来”。
points.enx: “Adjective + 下来” shows that a state begins and continues to develop, usually a change from movement to stillness or from strong to weak, e.g. 安静下来 (become quiet), 冷静下来 (calm down), 暗下来 (get dark).
egs: （1）太阳下山了，天渐渐暗下来了。
（2）听了老师的话，他慢慢冷静下来了。

points.name: 泼冷水
points.eg: 我呢，好像突然被人泼了一盆冷水，傻了。
points.egEn: As for me, I felt as if someone had suddenly thrown a basin of cold water over me—I was stunned.
points.zh: “泼冷水”，惯用语，本来指把冷水倒在别人身上，比喻打击别人的热情；“被泼了一盆冷水”也可以形容突然感到失望、清醒。
points.enx: “泼冷水” (literally “to pour cold water on”) is an idiomatic expression meaning to dampen someone's enthusiasm. “被泼了一盆冷水” can also describe suddenly feeling disappointed or sobered.
egs: （1）他正想去学画画，你别给他泼冷水。
（2）大家都很高兴，他却说了一些泼冷水的话。

think: 同学们为什么感谢我？
看到同学们都开始学习，我为什么想笑？

tf.q: 这个故事发生在四月二日。
“我”知道今天有英语测验。
同学们不相信“我”的话，都没有准备测验。
今天真的没有英语测验。
同学们很感谢“我”的帮助。

tip.title: 中国人过“洋节”
tip.zh: 随着中外交流越来越多，一些西方节日也在中国流行起来，人们把它们叫做“洋节”。圣诞节的时候，商场里摆着圣诞树，年轻人互相送礼物；2月14日情人节，街上到处都在卖玫瑰花和巧克力；愚人节的时候，朋友之间也喜欢开开玩笑。过洋节的大多是年轻人，对他们来说，这是和朋友一起放松、聚会的好机会。也有人担心洋节会影响传统节日，所以现在越来越多的人更加重视春节、端午节、七夕节等中国传统节日。
tip.en: As exchanges between China and other countries have increased, some Western festivals have become popular in China; people call them “foreign festivals”. At Christmas, shopping centres put up Christmas trees and young people give each other presents; on Valentine's Day, 14 February, roses and chocolates are on sale everywhere; and on April Fool's Day friends like to play jokes on each other. Most of the people who celebrate foreign festivals are young; for them these are good chances to relax and get together with friends. Some people worry that foreign festivals may affect traditional ones, so more and more people now pay greater attention to traditional Chinese festivals such as the Spring Festival, the Dragon Boat Festival and the Qixi Festival.

lessons.title: 电脑公司的清洁工
lessons.en: A Cleaner at a Computer Company
lessons.daodu: 每个人都能成功。重要的是，你能不能找到一条属于自己的成功之路。
lessons.daoduEn: Everyone can succeed. What matters is whether you can find a road to success that is your own.

paras.zh: 比西想去一家很大的电脑公司找一份工作。可是他没有什么特长，只能做打扫厕所的清洁工。
paras.py: Bǐxī xiǎng qù yì jiā hěn dà de diànnǎo gōngsī zhǎo yí fèn gōngzuò. Kěshì tā méiyǒu shénme tècháng, zhǐ néng zuò dǎsǎo cèsuǒ de qīngjiégōng.
paras.en: Bixi wanted to find a job at a big computer company. But he had no special skills and could only work as a cleaner, cleaning toilets.

paras.zh: 面试以后，公司的人员告诉他，在一起“考试”的十个人里，他打扫的厕所最干净，公司对他很满意。如果明天收到公司发给他的电子邮件，他就可以来上班了。
paras.py: Miànshì yǐhòu, gōngsī de rényuán gàosu tā, zài yìqǐ “kǎoshì” de shí gè rén li, tā dǎsǎo de cèsuǒ zuì gānjìng, gōngsī duì tā hěn mǎnyì. Rúguǒ míngtiān shōudào gōngsī fā gěi tā de diànzǐ yóujiàn, tā jiù kěyǐ lái shàngbān le.
paras.en: After the interview, the company staff told him that of the ten people who took the "test", he had cleaned the toilets best, and the company was very pleased with him. If he received an email from the company the next day, he could start work.

paras.zh: 这时候，他不好意思地说：“我没有电脑，也没有电子邮箱。”公司的人员吃惊地说：“没有告诉你，在这家公司，没有电子邮箱的人等于不存在，所以公司不能让他来工作。”比西非常失望。那时他身上只有十美元。他去商店买了十美元的土豆，然后到每家门口，问他们要不要买土豆。
paras.py: Zhè shíhou, tā bù hǎoyìsi de shuō: “Wǒ méiyǒu diànnǎo, yě méiyǒu diànzǐ yóuxiāng.” Gōngsī de rényuán chījīng de shuō: “Méiyǒu gàosu nǐ, zài zhè jiā gōngsī, méiyǒu diànzǐ yóuxiāng de rén děngyú bù cúnzài, suǒyǐ gōngsī bù néng ràng tā lái gōngzuò.” Bǐxī fēicháng shīwàng. Nà shí tā shēn shang zhǐyǒu shí měiyuán. Tā qù shāngdiàn mǎile shí měiyuán de tǔdòu, ránhòu dào měi jiā ménkǒu, wèn tāmen yào bu yào mǎi tǔdòu.
paras.en: Then he said, embarrassed: "I don't have a computer, or an email address." The staff member said in surprise: "(We) didn't tell you: at this company, a person without an email address doesn't exist, so the company can't let him work here." Bixi was very disappointed. He had only ten dollars on him. He went to a shop, bought ten dollars' worth of potatoes, and went door to door asking people if they wanted to buy potatoes.

paras.zh: 没想到，两个小时后他的土豆就卖光了。人们对这种送到家门口的土豆非常欢迎。他的手里一下子就有了二十美元。他开始认真地做这种生意。不停地努力加上一点儿运气，使他的生意越做越大，不但买了车，还请了二十多个工人。五年后，他建立了一个很大的公司。有了这个公司，人们在自己的家门口就可以买到新鲜的蔬菜。
paras.py: Méi xiǎngdào, liǎng gè xiǎoshí hòu tā de tǔdòu jiù màiguāng le. Rénmen duì zhè zhǒng sòngdào jiā ménkǒu de tǔdòu fēicháng huānyíng. Tā de shǒu li yíxiàzi jiù yǒule èrshí měiyuán. Tā kāishǐ rènzhēn de zuò zhè zhǒng shēngyi. Bù tíng de nǔlì jiāshang yìdiǎnr yùnqi, shǐ tā de shēngyi yuè zuò yuè dà, búdàn mǎile chē, hái qǐngle èrshí duō gè gōngrén. Wǔ nián hòu, tā jiànlìle yí gè hěn dà de gōngsī. Yǒule zhège gōngsī, rénmen zài zìjǐ de jiā ménkǒu jiù kěyǐ mǎidào xīnxiān de shūcài.
paras.en: To his surprise, his potatoes sold out in two hours. People really liked having potatoes delivered to their door. Suddenly he had twenty dollars in his hand. He started doing this business seriously. Constant hard work plus a little luck made his business grow and grow: he bought a truck and hired more than twenty workers. Five years later, he had built a big company. Thanks to it, people could buy fresh vegetables right at their own doors.

paras.zh: 一天，他去买保险。当保险公司的人问他的电子邮箱时，他再次说：“我没有电脑，也没有电子邮箱。”保险公司的人员说：“您有这样一个大公司，却没有电子邮箱。您想想，如果您有电子邮箱，用它可以做多少事！”
paras.py: Yì tiān, tā qù mǎi bǎoxiǎn. Dāng bǎoxiǎn gōngsī de rén wèn tā de diànzǐ yóuxiāng shí, tā zàicì shuō: “Wǒ méiyǒu diànnǎo, yě méiyǒu diànzǐ yóuxiāng.” Bǎoxiǎn gōngsī de rényuán shuō: “Nín yǒu zhèyàng yí gè dà gōngsī, què méiyǒu diànzǐ yóuxiāng. Nín xiǎngxiang, rúguǒ nín yǒu diànzǐ yóuxiāng, yòng tā kěyǐ zuò duōshao shì!”
paras.en: One day he went to buy insurance. When the insurance agent asked for his email address, he said again: "I don't have a computer, or an email address." The agent said: "You have such a big company, but no email address. Just think how much you could do if you had one!"

paras.zh: 他微笑着回答：“对，可以做电脑公司的清洁工。”
paras.py: Tā wēixiàozhe huídá: “Duì, kěyǐ zuò diànnǎo gōngsī de qīngjiégōng.”
paras.en: He smiled and answered: "Right - I could be a cleaner at a computer company."

points.name: 什么
points.eg: 可是他没有什么特长，只能做打扫厕所的清洁工。
points.egEn: But he had no special skills, so he could only work as a cleaner scrubbing toilets.
points.zh: “什么”在这里不表示疑问，而是表示虚指，“没有什么+名词”意思是“没有多少、没有特别的”，语气比较委婉。
points.enx: Here “什么” doesn't ask a question; it has an indefinite meaning. “没有什么 + noun” means “not much / nothing special”, a softer way of saying “not have”.
egs: （1）我今天没有什么事，可以陪你去买东西。
（2）这个电影没有什么意思，我们换一个吧。

points.name: 光
points.eg: 没想到，两个小时后他的土豆就卖光了。
points.egEn: Unexpectedly, his potatoes were sold out within two hours.
points.zh: “光”，形容词，用在动词后面作补语，表示一点儿也不剩，如“卖光、用光、吃光”。
points.enx: Here “光” is an adjective used after a verb as a complement, meaning “nothing left; all gone”, e.g. 卖光 (sold out), 用光 (used up), 吃光 (eaten up).
egs: （1）这个月的钱我已经花光了。
（2）孩子们很饿，一会儿就把饭菜吃光了。

think: 比西去那家电脑公司找工作时为什么没有被录用？
比西最后是怎么成功的？

tf.q: 比西去电脑公司工作，因为他打扫的厕所不干净。
比西去电脑公司找工作以前卖过土豆。
比西卖蔬菜挣了钱，当了老板。
现在比西有电子邮箱了。
比西觉得如果他有电子邮箱，就没有今天的成功。

mc.q: 根据短文，下面说法正确的是（ ）。
options: 电脑公司清洁工可以不会用电脑
离开电脑公司后，比西去卖保险了
人们不需要送到家门口的土豆
比西因为没有电子邮箱而不能在电脑公司工作

mc.q: 下面不是比西成功原因的是（ ）。
options: 能把新鲜蔬菜送到人们的家门口
认真地从小生意开始做
自己不停地努力，加上一点儿运气

tip.title: 晋商
tip.zh: 晋商就是山西商人，“晋”是山西省的简称。明清两代，晋商非常活跃，他们从贩卖盐和粮食开始，后来把生意做到了全国各地，甚至远到蒙古、俄罗斯，成为中国最有影响的商人群体之一。晋商讲究诚信，非常重视商业信誉。1823年，山西平遥出现了中国第一家票号“日升昌”，人们可以在这里存钱、汇款，它被称为中国现代银行的“鼻祖”。今天山西的乔家大院、王家大院等，都是当年晋商留下的住宅。
tip.en: The Jin merchants were merchants from Shanxi; “Jin” is the short name for Shanxi Province. During the Ming and Qing dynasties they were very active. Starting out by trading salt and grain, they later did business all over China and even as far away as Mongolia and Russia, becoming one of the most influential merchant groups in Chinese history. They valued honesty and took their business reputation very seriously. In 1823 China's first draft bank, Rishengchang, opened in Pingyao, Shanxi, where people could deposit and transfer money; it is called the “ancestor” of China's modern banks. The Qiao Family Compound, the Wang Family Compound and other mansions in Shanxi today were homes left behind by these merchants.

lessons.title: 这山望着那山高
lessons.py: Zhè shān wàngzhe nà shān gāo
lessons.en: The Grass Is Always Greener on the Other Side
lessons.daodu: 中国有句俗语，叫“这山望着那山高”，意思是爬上这座山，觉得另一座山更高。这句话是说人们总是对自己所处的环境不满意，认为别的地方会更好。
lessons.daoduEn: There is a Chinese saying, “From this mountain, that mountain looks higher.” It means that when you climb one mountain, another one seems higher. It describes how people are never satisfied with where they are and always think other places are better.

paras.zh: 一家女性婚姻介绍所开业了，女人们可以进去选择一个她喜欢的男人。介绍所门口有一个牌子，上面写着：
paras.py: Yì jiā nǚxìng hūnyīn jièshàosuǒ kāiyè le, nǚrénmen kěyǐ jìnqu xuǎnzé yí gè tā xǐhuan de nánrén. Jièshàosuǒ ménkǒu yǒu yí gè páizi, shàngmian xiězhe:
paras.en: A marriage agency for women opened, where women could go in and choose a man they liked. At the entrance was a sign that said:

paras.zh: 每个顾客只能进去一次！介绍所一共六层，越往上，男人的质量越高。不过请注意，顾客只能在任何一层挑一个丈夫或者继续上楼，但是不能回到以前到过的楼层。
paras.py: Měi gè gùkè zhǐ néng jìnqu yí cì! Jièshàosuǒ yígòng liù céng, yuè wǎng shàng, nánrén de zhìliàng yuè gāo. Búguò qǐng zhùyì, gùkè zhǐ néng zài rènhé yì céng tiāo yí gè zhàngfu huòzhě jìxù shàng lóu, dànshì bù néng huídào yǐqián dàoguo de lóucéng.
paras.en: Each customer may enter only once! The agency has six floors; the higher you go, the better the men. But please note: on any floor, a customer may only choose a husband there or keep going up - she cannot go back to a floor she has already visited.

paras.zh: 一个女人来到这儿想找一个丈夫。
paras.py: Yí gè nǚrén láidào zhèr xiǎng zhǎo yí gè zhàngfu.
paras.en: A woman came here hoping to find a husband.

paras.zh: 一层的门上这样写着：第一层，这里的男人有工作。女人还不满意，又上了第二层楼。
paras.py: Yī céng de mén shang zhèyàng xiězhe: Dì-yī céng, zhèlǐ de nánrén yǒu gōngzuò. Nǚrén hái bù mǎnyì, yòu shàngle dì-èr céng lóu.
paras.en: The door on the first floor said: "Floor 1: These men have jobs." The woman wasn't satisfied yet and went up to the second floor.

paras.zh: 二层的门上写着：第二层，这里的男人有工作而且喜欢小孩儿。女人停了一下，又上了第三层楼。
paras.py: Èr céng de mén shang xiězhe: Dì-èr céng, zhèlǐ de nánrén yǒu gōngzuò érqiě xǐhuan xiǎoháir. Nǚrén tíngle yíxià, yòu shàngle dì-sān céng lóu.
paras.en: The door on the second floor said: "Floor 2: These men have jobs and love children." The woman paused, then went up to the third floor.

paras.zh: 三层写着：第三层，这里的男人有工作，喜欢小孩儿，并且很帅。“啊！”她犹豫了一下，但还是往上走了。
paras.py: Sān céng xiězhe: Dì-sān céng, zhèlǐ de nánrén yǒu gōngzuò, xǐhuan xiǎoháir, bìngqiě hěn shuài. “À!” Tā yóuyùle yíxià, dàn háishi wǎng shàng zǒu le.
paras.en: The third floor said: "Floor 3: These men have jobs, love children, and are handsome." "Oh!" She hesitated, but kept going up.

paras.zh: 四层写着：第四层，这里的男人有工作，喜欢小孩儿，不但非常帅，还会帮助太太做家务。“天啊！”女人叫道，“我快站不住了！”然后，她还是爬上了第五层楼。
paras.py: Sì céng xiězhe: Dì-sì céng, zhèlǐ de nánrén yǒu gōngzuò, xǐhuan xiǎoháir, búdàn fēicháng shuài, hái huì bāngzhù tàitai zuò jiāwù. “Tiān a!” Nǚrén jiàodào, “Wǒ kuài zhàn bú zhù le!” Ránhòu, tā háishi páshangle dì-wǔ céng lóu.
paras.en: The fourth floor said: "Floor 4: These men have jobs, love children, are very handsome, and also help their wives with housework." "Oh my!" the woman cried. "I can hardly stand!" Still, she climbed up to the fifth floor.

paras.zh: 她读着五层的说明书：第五层，这里的男人有工作，喜欢小孩儿，也非常帅，还会做家务，并且非常浪漫。女人非常想留在这一层，但是充满期待地走向最高一层。
paras.py: Tā dúzhe wǔ céng de shuōmíngshū: Dì-wǔ céng, zhèlǐ de nánrén yǒu gōngzuò, xǐhuan xiǎoháir, yě fēicháng shuài, hái huì zuò jiāwù, bìngqiě fēicháng làngmàn. Nǚrén fēicháng xiǎng liú zài zhè yì céng, dànshì chōngmǎn qīdài de zǒuxiàng zuì gāo yì céng.
paras.en: She read the notice on the fifth floor: "Floor 5: These men have jobs, love children, are very handsome, do housework, and are very romantic." The woman badly wanted to stay on this floor, but, full of hope, she headed for the top floor.

paras.zh: 六层出现了一个很大的电子牌，上面写着：你是这层楼的第456021位客人。这里没有任何男人，这层楼只是为了证明女人是多么难以满足。
paras.py: Liù céng chūxiànle yí gè hěn dà de diànzǐpái, shàngmian xiězhe: Nǐ shì zhè céng lóu de dì 456021 wèi kèrén. Zhèlǐ méiyǒu rènhé nánrén, zhè céng lóu zhǐ shì wèile zhèngmíng nǚrén shì duōme nányǐ mǎnzú.
paras.en: On the sixth floor was a big electronic sign that said: "You are visitor number 456,021 to this floor. There are no men here. This floor exists only to prove how hard women are to satisfy."

paras.zh: 不久，一家男性婚姻介绍所在街对面开业了，经营方式与前一个几乎一样。
paras.py: Bùjiǔ, yì jiā nánxìng hūnyīn jièshàosuǒ zài jiē duìmiàn kāiyè le, jīngyíng fāngshì yǔ qián yí gè jīhū yíyàng.
paras.en: Soon after, a marriage agency for men opened across the street, run in almost exactly the same way.

paras.zh: 第一层的女人长得漂亮。
paras.py: Dì-yī céng de nǚrén zhǎng de piàoliang.
paras.en: Floor 1: The women are pretty.

paras.zh: 第二层的女人长得漂亮而且有钱……
paras.py: Dì-èr céng de nǚrén zhǎng de piàoliang érqiě yǒu qián...
paras.en: Floor 2: The women are pretty and rich...

paras.zh: 结果，第三层到第六层从来没有男人上去过。
paras.py: Jiéguǒ, dì-sān céng dào dì-liù céng cónglái méiyǒu nánrén shàngqu guo.
paras.en: As a result, no man ever went up to floors 3 through 6.

points.name: 越……越……
points.eg: 介绍所一共六层，越往上，男人的质量越高。
points.egEn: The agency has six floors in all; the higher you go, the better the quality of the men.
points.zh: “越A越B”表示B随着A的变化而变化，A、B可以是动词、形容词或短语。
points.enx: “越A越B” means “the more A, the more B”: B changes as A changes. A and B can be verbs, adjectives or phrases.
egs: （1）这本小说我越看越喜欢。
（2）雨越下越大，我们只好回家了。

points.name: 难以
points.eg: 这层楼只是为了证明女人是多么难以满足。
points.egEn: This floor exists only to prove how hard women are to satisfy.
points.zh: “难以”，意思是“不容易、很难”，后面常跟双音节动词，多用于书面语，如“难以满足”“难以想象”。
points.enx: “难以” means “difficult to; hard to”. It is usually followed by a two-syllable verb and is mostly used in written Chinese, e.g. 难以满足 (hard to satisfy), 难以想象 (hard to imagine).
egs: （1）这么大的变化，真让人难以相信。
（2）他说的话让人难以理解。

think: 这家婚姻介绍所对顾客的要求是什么？
那个女人找到满意的丈夫了吗？为什么？
男性婚姻介绍所的情况怎么解释？

mc.q: 关于女性婚姻介绍所，下面说法正确的是（ ）。
options: 高层的男人质量不如低层的男人
上到高层以后还可以再回到低层
最高层有条件最好的男人

mc.q: 从那个女人到这家婚姻介绍所的情况，我们可以知道（ ）。
options: 她对第五层的男人没有一点儿兴趣
已经有很多女人来过第六层
第六层的男人都被别人选走了
很多女人在这里找到了丈夫

mc.q: 这个故事想说明（ ）。
options: 对男人的期待应该高一些
男人不喜欢有钱的女人

tip.title: 中国的俗语
tip.zh: 俗语是在老百姓中流传的、通俗易懂的固定语句，大多是人们从生活经验中总结出来的。它们语言简单、形象生动，常常一句话就能说明一个道理。比如“这山望着那山高”说人总不满足，“三个臭皮匠，顶个诸葛亮”说人多办法多，“一口吃不成胖子”说做事不能着急。俗语和成语不一样：成语大多是四个字，很多来自古书和历史故事，比如“画蛇添足”；俗语则更加口语化。学会用俗语，能让你的汉语更地道。
tip.en: Common sayings are fixed, easy-to-understand expressions passed around among ordinary people, mostly summed up from everyday experience. Their language is simple and vivid, and a single saying can often explain a whole lesson about life. For example, “From this mountain, that mountain looks higher” says people are never satisfied; “Three cobblers together equal one Zhuge Liang” says many people have many ideas; and “You can't get fat on one mouthful” says you shouldn't be in a hurry. Sayings are different from chengyu: chengyu are mostly four characters long and many come from ancient books and historical stories, such as “drawing legs on a snake”, while sayings are more colloquial. Learning to use sayings will make your Chinese more natural.

lessons.title: 送东西
lessons.daodu: 郑板桥是中国清朝的著名人物。他既是一位画家，又是一位关心人民生活的好官。
lessons.daoduEn: Zheng Banqiao was a famous figure of the Qing Dynasty. He was both a painter and a good official who cared about the lives of ordinary people.

paras.zh: 有一年春节，郑板桥陪着一个官员出门办事。路上，有一家人的门上贴着这样一副对联：
paras.py: Yǒu yì nián Chūnjié, Zhèng Bǎnqiáo péizhe yí gè guānyuán chūmén bànshì. Lù shang, yǒu yì jiā rén de mén shang tiēzhe zhèyàng yí fù duìlián:
paras.en: One Spring Festival, Zheng Banqiao went out on business with an official. On the way, they saw a pair of couplets on a family's door:

paras.zh: 上联：二三四五
paras.py: Shànglián: Èr sān sì wǔ
paras.en: First line: Two, three, four, five

paras.zh: 下联：六七八九
paras.py: Xiàlián: Liù qī bā jiǔ
paras.en: Second line: Six, seven, eight, nine

paras.zh: 横批：南北
paras.py: Héngpī: Nán běi
paras.en: Horizontal scroll: South, North

paras.zh: 郑板桥看到这副对联后，马上往回走。过了一会儿，他拿着几件衣服，一些肉和菜，还有一些粮食回来了。他推开这家人的大门，看见一家人都挤在一张床上，穿着很少的衣服，而厨房里什么吃的东西都没有。郑板桥对他们说：“春节到了，我带了这些东西给你们。你们用吧！”那家人看到这些东西，非常感动，也非常高兴，连忙向郑板桥道谢。
paras.py: Zhèng Bǎnqiáo kàndào zhè fù duìlián hòu, mǎshàng wǎng huí zǒu. Guòle yíhuìr, tā názhe jǐ jiàn yīfu, yìxiē ròu hé cài, hái yǒu yìxiē liángshi huílai le. Tā tuīkāi zhè jiā rén de dàmén, kànjiàn yì jiā rén dōu jǐ zài yì zhāng chuáng shang, chuānzhe hěn shǎo de yīfu, ér chúfáng li shénme chī de dōngxi dōu méiyǒu. Zhèng Bǎnqiáo duì tāmen shuō: “Chūnjié dào le, wǒ dàile zhèxiē dōngxi gěi nǐmen. Nǐmen yòng ba!” Nà jiā rén kàndào zhèxiē dōngxi, fēicháng gǎndòng, yě fēicháng gāoxìng, liánmáng xiàng Zhèng Bǎnqiáo dàoxiè.
paras.en: After seeing these couplets, Zheng Banqiao immediately turned back. A while later he returned with some clothes, some meat and vegetables, and some grain. He pushed open the family's gate and saw the whole family squeezed together on one bed, wearing very few clothes, and there was nothing at all to eat in the kitchen. Zheng Banqiao said to them: "The Spring Festival is here. I've brought you these things. Please use them!" When the family saw these things, they were deeply moved and very happy, and thanked him again and again.

paras.zh: 等到郑板桥和官员出了这家的门，官员问他：“你怎么知道这家人没有衣服，也没有吃的东西呢？”
paras.py: Děngdào Zhèng Bǎnqiáo hé guānyuán chūle zhè jiā de mén, guānyuán wèn tā: “Nǐ zěnme zhīdào zhè jiā rén méiyǒu yīfu, yě méiyǒu chī de dōngxi ne?”
paras.en: When Zheng Banqiao and the official had left the house, the official asked him: "How did you know this family had no clothes and nothing to eat?"

paras.zh: 郑板桥指着这家门上的对联说：“上联‘二三四五’，里面没有‘一’（和‘衣’读音相同）。下联‘六七八九’，里面没有‘十’（和‘食’读音相同）。应该是‘缺衣少食’四个字的意思，横批却只写了‘南北’，就是没有‘东西’，这个对联不就是告诉我们，他们家缺衣少食，没有东西过春节吗？”
paras.py: Zhèng Bǎnqiáo zhǐzhe zhè jiā mén shang de duìlián shuō: “Shànglián ‘èr sān sì wǔ’, lǐmiàn méiyǒu ‘yī’ (hé ‘yī’ dúyīn xiāngtóng). Xiàlián ‘liù qī bā jiǔ’, lǐmiàn méiyǒu ‘shí’ (hé ‘shí’ dúyīn xiāngtóng). Yīnggāi shì ‘quē yī shǎo shí’ sì gè zì de yìsi, héngpī què zhǐ xiěle ‘nán běi’, jiù shì méiyǒu ‘dōng xī’, zhège duìlián bú jiù shì gàosu wǒmen, tāmen jiā quē yī shǎo shí, méiyǒu dōngxi guò Chūnjié ma?”
paras.en: Zheng Banqiao pointed to the couplets on the door and said: "The first line, 'two, three, four, five', is missing 'one' (一 yī, which sounds the same as 衣 yī, 'clothes'). The second line, 'six, seven, eight, nine', is missing 'ten' (十 shí, which sounds the same as 食 shí, 'food'). So it means 缺衣少食, 'short of clothes and food'. And the horizontal scroll says only 'South, North' - that is, no 'East, West' (东西 dōngxi also means 'things'). Aren't the couplets telling us that the family lacks clothes and food and has nothing to celebrate the Spring Festival with?"

points.name: 等到
points.eg: 等到郑板桥和官员出了这家的门，官员问他……
points.egEn: When Zheng Banqiao and the official had come out of the house, the official asked him...
points.zh: “等到”表示“到了某个时候”，后面常跟一个短语或分句，说明后面的事情在这个时候发生。
points.enx: “等到” means “when; by the time; until”. It is followed by a phrase or clause indicating the time at which the next event happens.
egs: （1）等到我们赶到车站，火车已经开走了。
（2）等到春天来了，我们一起去爬山吧。

points.name: 缺
points.eg: 这个对联不就是告诉我们，他们家缺衣少食，没有东西过春节吗？
points.egEn: Isn't this couplet telling us that their family is short of clothes and food and has nothing to celebrate the Spring Festival with?
points.zh: “缺”，动词，表示缺少、不够，后面常跟名词，如“缺钱”“缺人”。“缺衣少食”是说没有足够的衣服和食物。
points.enx: “缺” is a verb meaning “to lack; to be short of”, often followed by a noun, e.g. 缺钱 (short of money), 缺人 (short-handed). “缺衣少食” means not having enough clothes or food.
egs: （1）我们公司现在很缺会说汉语的人。
（2）这个地方很缺水，人们生活很不方便。

think: 郑板桥怎么知道那家人生活情况呢？
那家人的生活怎么样？

tf.q: 郑板桥陪着那个官员回家过春节。
郑板桥认识那家人。
那个官员没有明白那副对联的真正意思。
郑板桥很聪明而且很愿意帮助别人。

tip.title: 对联
tip.zh: 对联也叫“对子”，是中国特有的一种文学形式，由上联和下联组成，有时再加上横批。对联要求上下联字数相同，词性和意思相对，比如“天”对“地”，“山”对“水”。按照传统，上联最后一个字一般是仄声，下联最后一个字一般是平声。贴的时候，上联贴在门的右边，下联贴在左边，横批贴在门的上面。春节时贴的对联叫“春联”，一般写在红纸上，表达人们对新一年的美好祝愿。
tip.en: Couplets, also called “duizi”, are a literary form unique to China. A couplet consists of a first line and a second line, sometimes with a horizontal scroll added. The two lines must have the same number of characters, and their words must match in part of speech and correspond in meaning, e.g. “sky” with “earth”, “mountain” with “water”. Traditionally, the last character of the first line has an oblique tone and that of the second line a level tone. When they are pasted up, the first line goes on the right of the door, the second on the left and the horizontal scroll above the door. Couplets put up for the Spring Festival are called “chunlian”; they are usually written on red paper and express good wishes for the new year.

lessons.title: 勇敢地说“不”
lessons.daodu: 能够对别人说“不”，其实需要很大的勇气。
lessons.daoduEn: Being able to say “no” to others actually takes a lot of courage.

paras.zh: 马南最近刚刚参加工作，他的姑妈来这个城市看他。马南陪着姑妈在这个小城市里转了转，就到了吃饭的时间。
paras.py: Mǎ Nán zuìjìn gānggāng cānjiā gōngzuò, tā de gūmā lái zhège chéngshì kàn tā. Mǎ Nán péizhe gūmā zài zhège xiǎo chéngshì li zhuànle zhuàn, jiù dàole chīfàn de shíjiān.
paras.en: Ma Nan had just started working, and his aunt came to the city to visit him. He showed her around the small city, and then it was time to eat.

paras.zh: 姑妈一直对他很好，马南想请她好好吃一顿，可他身上只有20块钱。只好在一个小饭馆里随便吃一点儿。但是，姑妈却带他走进了一家很讲究的餐厅。马南没办法，只好跟着她走了进去。
paras.py: Gūmā yìzhí duì tā hěn hǎo, Mǎ Nán xiǎng qǐng tā hǎohāo chī yí dùn, kě tā shēn shang zhǐyǒu 20 kuài qián. Zhǐhǎo zài yí gè xiǎo fànguǎn li suíbiàn chī yìdiǎnr. Dànshì, gūmā què dài tā zǒujìnle yì jiā hěn jiǎngjiu de cāntīng. Mǎ Nán méi bànfǎ, zhǐhǎo gēnzhe tā zǒule jìnqu.
paras.en: His aunt had always been very good to him, and Ma Nan wanted to treat her to a really nice meal, but he had only 20 yuan on him. He could only have a simple bite at a small restaurant. But his aunt took him into a very fancy restaurant. Ma Nan had no choice but to follow her in.

paras.zh: 两人坐下来后，姑妈开始点菜。当她问马南吃什么时，马南只是吞吞吐吐地说：“随便，随便。”这时，他的心中七上八下，放在口袋里的手紧紧抓着那20块钱。这些钱显然是不够的，怎么办？
paras.py: Liǎng rén zuò xiàlai hòu, gūmā kāishǐ diǎn cài. Dāng tā wèn Mǎ Nán chī shénme shí, Mǎ Nán zhǐshì tūntūntǔtǔ de shuō: “Suíbiàn, suíbiàn.” Zhè shí, tā de xīn zhōng qī shàng bā xià, fàng zài kǒudai li de shǒu jǐnjǐn zhuāzhe nà 20 kuài qián. Zhèxiē qián xiǎnrán shì bú gòu de, zěnme bàn?
paras.en: After they sat down, his aunt began to order. When she asked Ma Nan what he wanted to eat, he just mumbled: "Anything, anything." His heart was pounding with worry, and his hand in his pocket gripped the 20 yuan tightly. This money was clearly not enough. What should he do?

paras.zh: 可是姑妈一点儿也没注意到马南的不安，她不停地说着这儿的饭菜多么好吃，马南却什么味道都没吃出来。
paras.py: Kěshì gūmā yìdiǎnr yě méi zhùyì dào Mǎ Nán de bù'ān, tā bù tíng de shuōzhe zhèr de fàncài duōme hǎochī, Mǎ Nán què shénme wèidao dōu méi chī chūlai.
paras.en: But his aunt didn't notice Ma Nan's unease at all. She kept saying how delicious the food was, while Ma Nan couldn't taste anything.

paras.zh: 结账的时候终于到了，服务员拿着账单向马南走来。马南张开嘴，却什么也说不出来。
paras.py: Jiézhàng de shíhou zhōngyú dào le, fúwùyuán názhe zhàngdān xiàng Mǎ Nán zǒulái. Mǎ Nán zhāngkāi zuǐ, què shénme yě shuō bù chūlai.
paras.en: Finally it was time to pay, and the waiter came toward Ma Nan with the bill. Ma Nan opened his mouth, but couldn't say a word.

paras.zh: 姑妈笑了。她拿过账单，把钱给了服务员，然后对马南说：“孩子，我知道你的感觉。我一直在等你说‘不’，可你为什么不说呢？要知道，有些时候一定要勇敢地把这个字说出来，才是最好的选择。我这次来，就是想让你明白这个道理。”
paras.py: Gūmā xiào le. Tā náguo zhàngdān, bǎ qián gěile fúwùyuán, ránhòu duì Mǎ Nán shuō: “Háizi, wǒ zhīdào nǐ de gǎnjué. Wǒ yìzhí zài děng nǐ shuō ‘bù’, kě nǐ wèishénme bù shuō ne? Yào zhīdào, yǒuxiē shíhou yídìng yào yǒnggǎn de bǎ zhège zì shuō chūlai, cái shì zuì hǎo de xuǎnzé. Wǒ zhè cì lái, jiù shì xiǎng ràng nǐ míngbai zhège dàoli.”
paras.en: His aunt smiled. She took the bill, gave the money to the waiter, and said to Ma Nan: "My boy, I know how you feel. I've been waiting for you to say 'no' - why didn't you? You see, sometimes having the courage to say that word is the best choice. That's why I came this time: to help you understand this."

points.name: 显然
points.eg: 这些钱显然是不够的，怎么办？
points.egEn: This money was obviously not enough. What should he do?
points.zh: “显然”，形容词，表示事情或道理很容易看出来、非常明显，常作状语，用在句首或动词前。
points.enx: “显然” means “obviously; clearly”. It is mostly used adverbially, at the beginning of a sentence or before the verb.
egs: （1）他一句话也不说，显然是生气了。
（2）显然，这个办法比原来的好多了。

points.name: 什么……都/也……
points.eg: 她不停地说着这儿的饭菜多么好吃，马南却什么味道都没吃出来。
points.egEn: She kept talking about how delicious the food there was, but Ma Nan couldn't taste anything at all.
points.zh: “什么……都/也……”表示任指，强调在说到的范围内没有例外，否定句中常用“什么……也/都+不/没……”。
points.enx: “什么……都/也……” has an all-inclusive meaning (“anything / nothing at all”), stressing that there are no exceptions. In negative sentences it becomes “什么……也/都 + 不/没……”.
egs: （1）他太累了，回到家什么也不想做。
（2）我刚来中国的时候，看到什么都觉得新鲜。

think: 结账的时候，发生了什么事？
点菜的时候，马南为什么吞吞吐吐？
你觉得马南为什么一直没有对姑妈说“不”？

tf.q: 马南已经工作了很多年。
马南身上钱不多，所以不能去很好的饭馆。
最后，付钱的是马南。

mc.q: “马南的心中七上八下”的意思是（ ）。
马南什么味道都没吃出来，是因为（ ）。
姑妈要去那家很讲究的饭馆，是因为（ ）。
options: 那家饭馆的菜非常好吃
她知道马南去那家饭馆
她想让马南明白一个道理
她太饿了就随便找了一家饭馆

tip.title: 面子
tip.zh: “面子”本来是脸的意思，后来指一个人的尊严、名誉和在别人眼中的形象。中国人很重视面子，汉语里有很多和面子有关的说法：“有面子”是受到尊重、感到光荣；“丢面子”是在别人面前出丑；“给面子”是尊重对方，不让对方难堪；“爱面子”是特别在意别人怎么看自己。比如请客吃饭时，主人总希望菜多一些、好一些，觉得这样才有面子。不过，太爱面子也会让人勉强自己，就像课文里的马南一样。
tip.en: “Mianzi” originally meant “face”, and later came to mean a person's dignity, reputation and image in other people's eyes. Chinese people care a great deal about face, and Chinese has many expressions about it: “to have face” means to be respected and feel honoured; “to lose face” means to be embarrassed in front of others; “to give face” means to show respect and not embarrass someone; and “to love face” means to care very much about how others see you. When treating guests to a meal, for example, the host always wants more and better dishes, feeling that this gives him face. But caring too much about face can make people force themselves to do things, just like Ma Nan in the text.

lessons.title: 第一笔工资
lessons.daodu: 几个不同国家的人，说着不同的语言，他们在一起能交流吗？
lessons.daoduEn: Can people from several different countries, speaking different languages, communicate with each other?

paras.zh: 我十六岁的时候到美国上中学。那时我第一次出去打工，工作很简单，只是把气球包装一下，然后装在箱子里运走。但是在简单的工作中我却得到了一笔丰厚的“工资”。
paras.py: Wǒ shíliù suì de shíhou dào Měiguó shàng zhōngxué. Nà shí wǒ dì-yī cì chūqu dǎgōng, gōngzuò hěn jiǎndān, zhǐshì bǎ qìqiú bāozhuāng yíxià, ránhòu zhuāng zài xiāngzi li yùnzǒu. Dànshì zài jiǎndān de gōngzuò zhōng wǒ què dédàole yì bǐ fēnghòu de “gōngzī”.
paras.en: When I was sixteen, I went to the US for high school. That was when I took my first part-time job. The work was very simple: just packing balloons and putting them in boxes to be shipped. But from this simple job I earned a rich "salary".

paras.zh: 所有的“工人”加起来只有六个人，但是很热闹。原因很简单——我们说三种不同的语言：两个是美国的“ABC”（American Born Chinese，在美国出生的中国人），说英语；两个是刚到美国的中国人，说汉语；还有两个是墨西哥人，当然说西班牙语了。这样的六个人到了一起会怎么样呢？结果是我们居然交流得很顺畅。每个人好像都忘了对方听不懂自己的语言。两个墨西哥男孩儿好几次都用西班牙语向我问事情，而另一个中国女孩儿有时也对他们说中国话。但奇怪的是，我们竟然没有一次把对方的话理解错。不光如此，我们有时还聊得很高兴，常常大声地笑起来。
paras.py: Suǒyǒu de “gōngrén” jiā qǐlai zhǐyǒu liù gè rén, dànshì hěn rènao. Yuányīn hěn jiǎndān —— wǒmen shuō sān zhǒng bù tóng de yǔyán: liǎng gè shì Měiguó de “ABC” (American Born Chinese, zài Měiguó chūshēng de Zhōngguórén), shuō Yīngyǔ; liǎng gè shì gāng dào Měiguó de Zhōngguórén, shuō Hànyǔ; hái yǒu liǎng gè shì Mòxīgērén, dāngrán shuō Xībānyáyǔ le. Zhèyàng de liù gè rén dàole yìqǐ huì zěnmeyàng ne? Jiéguǒ shì wǒmen jūrán jiāoliú de hěn shùnchàng. Měi gè rén hǎoxiàng dōu wàngle duìfāng tīng bù dǒng zìjǐ de yǔyán. Liǎng gè Mòxīgē nánháir hǎo jǐ cì dōu yòng Xībānyáyǔ xiàng wǒ wèn shìqing, ér lìng yí gè Zhōngguó nǚháir yǒushí yě duì tāmen shuō Zhōngguóhuà. Dàn qíguài de shì, wǒmen jìngrán méiyǒu yí cì bǎ duìfāng de huà lǐjiě cuò. Bùguāng rúcǐ, wǒmen yǒushí hái liáo de hěn gāoxìng, chángcháng dàshēng de xiào qǐlai.
paras.en: There were only six "workers" in all, but it was lively. The reason was simple - we spoke three different languages: two were American "ABCs" (American Born Chinese) who spoke English; two were Chinese who had just arrived in the US and spoke Chinese; and two were Mexicans who, of course, spoke Spanish. What happens when six people like that get together? Amazingly, we communicated very smoothly. Everyone seemed to forget that the others couldn't understand their language. The two Mexican boys asked me things in Spanish several times, and the other Chinese girl sometimes spoke Chinese to them. But strangely, we never once misunderstood each other. What's more, we sometimes chatted happily and often burst out laughing.

paras.zh: 这种交流不能不说是奇特的。但是静下心来想一想，也没有什么奇怪的。语言只是人们交流的工具。它帮助你了解别人，同时也让别人了解你。我们虽然使用着不同的“工具”，但是说话交流的心情却是一样的。这使我们之间有了一种默契。我喜欢这种默契，它就是我第一次打工的“工资”，非常丰厚！
paras.py: Zhè zhǒng jiāoliú bù néng bù shuō shì qítè de. Dànshì jìng xià xīn lai xiǎng yi xiǎng, yě méiyǒu shénme qíguài de. Yǔyán zhǐshì rénmen jiāoliú de gōngjù. Tā bāngzhù nǐ liǎojiě biérén, tóngshí yě ràng biérén liǎojiě nǐ. Wǒmen suīrán shǐyòngzhe bù tóng de “gōngjù”, dànshì shuōhuà jiāoliú de xīnqíng què shì yíyàng de. Zhè shǐ wǒmen zhījiān yǒule yì zhǒng mòqì. Wǒ xǐhuan zhè zhǒng mòqì, tā jiù shì wǒ dì-yī cì dǎgōng de “gōngzī”, fēicháng fēnghòu!
paras.en: You have to admit this kind of communication was unusual. But if you calm down and think about it, it's not so strange. Language is just a tool for communication. It helps you understand others and helps others understand you. Although we used different "tools", our wish to talk and connect was the same. That gave us an unspoken understanding. I love that understanding - it was the "salary" from my first job, and a very rich one!

points.name: 不光如此
points.eg: 不光如此，我们有时还聊得很高兴。
points.egEn: Not only that, sometimes we even chatted happily together.
points.zh: “不光如此”意思是“不仅这样”，用在后一句的开头，表示在前面说的情况之外，还有更进一步的情况，后面常用“还、也”。
points.enx: “不光如此” means “not only that; besides”. It begins a following sentence and adds a further point beyond what was said before; 还 or 也 often follows.
egs: （1）这家饭馆的菜很好吃，不光如此，价格也很便宜。
（2）他会说汉语，不光如此，还会写很多汉字。

points.name: 使
points.eg: 这使我们之间有了一种默契。
points.egEn: This created a kind of tacit understanding between us.
points.zh: “使”，动词，意思是“让、叫”，常用格式“A使B+动词/形容词”，表示A造成B发生某种变化，多用于书面语。
points.enx: “使” is a verb meaning “to make; to cause”. In the pattern “A使B + verb/adjective” it shows that A brings about a change in B. It is mostly used in written Chinese.
egs: （1）这次旅行使我认识了很多新朋友。
（2）他的话使大家都笑了起来。

think: 我为什么到美国去？
我第一次打工的工作是什么？
我们六个人能不能交流？为什么？

tf.q: 我十六岁的时候到美国去工作。
我第一次去打工，挣了很多钱。
一起工作的六个人都说英语。

mc.q: “这种交流不能不说是奇特的”，这句话的意思是（ ）。
options: 这种交流很奇怪，而且特别
这种交流不算奇怪，也不特别
这种交流没有一点儿问题

mc.q: “我们竟然没有一次把对方的话理解错”，这句话的意思是（ ）。
options: 我们只有一次理解错了
我们只有一次理解对了

mc.q: 在“我们虽然使用着不同的‘工具’”中，“工具”指的是（ ）。

tip.title: 剪纸艺术
tip.zh: 剪纸是中国最古老的民间艺术之一，已经有一千多年的历史。人们用剪刀或刻刀在纸上剪出各种图案，比如花鸟、动物、人物和吉祥的文字。剪纸大多用红纸，因为红色在中国代表喜庆和吉祥。春节的时候，人们把剪好的“窗花”贴在窗户上；结婚的时候，家里会贴上大红的“囍”字。剪纸不仅用来装饰，也表达了人们对美好生活的希望。2009年，中国剪纸被列入联合国教科文组织人类非物质文化遗产代表作名录。
tip.en: Paper-cutting is one of China's oldest folk arts, with a history of more than a thousand years. People use scissors or carving knives to cut all kinds of patterns out of paper—flowers and birds, animals, figures and auspicious characters. Red paper is used most, because red stands for joy and good fortune in China. At the Spring Festival people paste paper-cut “window flowers” on their windows, and at a wedding the home is decorated with a big red “double happiness” character. Paper-cuts are not only decorations but also express people's hopes for a good life. In 2009, Chinese paper-cutting was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

lessons.title: 中国人最喜欢的运动
lessons.daodu: 你知道中国的“国球”是什么吗？
lessons.daoduEn: Do you know what China's “national ball game” is?

paras.zh: 在中国，你知道人们最喜欢哪种运动吗？不是篮球，不是足球，而是乒乓球！
paras.py: Zài Zhōngguó, nǐ zhīdào rénmen zuì xǐhuan nǎ zhǒng yùndòng ma? Bú shì lánqiú, bú shì zúqiú, ér shì pīngpāngqiú!
paras.en: Do you know which sport people in China like best? Not basketball, not soccer, but table tennis!

paras.zh: 1904年，一个上海老板从日本买回10套乒乓球器材，乒乓球运动从此传入中国。自从1959年中国运动员容国团获得第一个世界冠军后，乒乓球运动在中国发展非常快，并成为中国的“国球”。
paras.py: 1904 nián, yí gè Shànghǎi lǎobǎn cóng Rìběn mǎi huí 10 tào pīngpāngqiú qìcái, pīngpāngqiú yùndòng cóngcǐ chuánrù Zhōngguó. Zìcóng 1959 nián Zhōngguó yùndòngyuán Róng Guótuán huòdé dì-yī gè shìjiè guànjūn hòu, pīngpāngqiú yùndòng zài Zhōngguó fāzhǎn fēicháng kuài, bìng chéngwéi Zhōngguó de “guóqiú”.
paras.en: In 1904, a Shanghai businessman bought 10 sets of table tennis equipment from Japan, and the sport came to China. After the Chinese player Rong Guotuan won China's first world championship in 1959, table tennis developed very quickly in China and became China's "national sport".

paras.zh: 乒乓球的重量虽然很轻，但是它在中国人心中却是很重很重的。小学生、初中生、高中生和大学生，都喜欢在课间和课后打乒乓球；其他人也经常在休息的时候打乒乓球。
paras.py: Pīngpāngqiú de zhòngliàng suīrán hěn qīng, dànshì tā zài Zhōngguórén xīn zhōng què shì hěn zhòng hěn zhòng de. Xiǎoxuéshēng, chūzhōngshēng, gāozhōngshēng hé dàxuéshēng, dōu xǐhuan zài kèjiān hé kèhòu dǎ pīngpāngqiú; qítā rén yě jīngcháng zài xiūxi de shíhou dǎ pīngpāngqiú.
paras.en: A table tennis ball is very light, but it weighs very, very heavily in Chinese hearts. Primary, middle school, high school and university students all like to play table tennis between and after classes, and other people often play in their free time too.

paras.zh: 每到奥运会举行的时候，中国人都盼望着看到乒乓球比赛，因为他们能够欣赏到运动员的精彩表现。如果你认为中国人只是喜欢自己国家的运动员，那你就错了。中国人也很喜欢看其他国家选手的比赛。为了观看精彩的乒乓球比赛，中国观众可以在电视机前坐上好几个小时！
paras.py: Měi dào Àoyùnhuì jǔxíng de shíhou, Zhōngguórén dōu pànwàngzhe kàndào pīngpāngqiú bǐsài, yīnwèi tāmen nénggòu xīnshǎng dào yùndòngyuán de jīngcǎi biǎoxiàn. Rúguǒ nǐ rènwéi Zhōngguórén zhǐshì xǐhuan zìjǐ guójiā de yùndòngyuán, nà nǐ jiù cuò le. Zhōngguórén yě hěn xǐhuan kàn qítā guójiā xuǎnshǒu de bǐsài. Wèile guānkàn jīngcǎi de pīngpāngqiú bǐsài, Zhōngguó guānzhòng kěyǐ zài diànshìjī qián zuòshang hǎo jǐ gè xiǎoshí!
paras.en: Whenever the Olympics are held, Chinese people look forward to the table tennis matches, because they can enjoy the players' brilliant performances. If you think Chinese people only like their own country's players, you're wrong. They also love watching players from other countries. To watch exciting table tennis, Chinese viewers will sit in front of the TV for hours!

paras.zh: 现在，中国人希望有更多的外国朋友能够喜欢这个运动，希望更多的外国朋友打乒乓球，也希望大家能够一起享受这个运动的乐趣！
paras.py: Xiànzài, Zhōngguórén xīwàng yǒu gèng duō de wàiguó péngyou nénggòu xǐhuan zhège yùndòng, xīwàng gèng duō de wàiguó péngyou dǎ pīngpāngqiú, yě xīwàng dàjiā nénggòu yìqǐ xiǎngshòu zhège yùndòng de lèqù!
paras.en: Now Chinese people hope that more foreign friends will come to like this sport and play table tennis, and that everyone can enjoy its fun together!

points.name: 每到
points.eg: 每到奥运会举行的时候，中国人都盼望着看到乒乓球比赛。
points.egEn: Whenever the Olympic Games are held, Chinese people look forward to watching the table tennis matches.
points.zh: “每到……（的时候）”表示每次到了某个时间或情况，后面常用“都、总”，说明有规律地重复出现的事情。
points.enx: “每到……（的时候）” means “whenever; every time (a certain time comes)”. It is usually followed by 都 or 总 and describes something that happens regularly.
egs: （1）每到春节，在外地工作的人都要回家和家人团聚。
（2）每到周末，这个公园里总有很多人。

points.name: 坐上好几个小时
points.eg: 中国观众可以在电视机前坐上好几个小时！
points.egEn: Chinese viewers can sit in front of the TV for hours!
points.zh: “动词+上+数量”表示动作达到或持续了一定的数量或时间，“好几个小时”强调时间长。
points.enx: “Verb + 上 + quantity” shows that an action reaches or lasts a certain amount or length of time. “好几个小时” (quite a few hours) stresses that the time is long.
egs: （1）他一看起书来，就能看上一整天。
（2）这个电影很长，要看上三个小时。

think: 乒乓球运动是怎样传入中国的？
中国人为什么爱看乒乓球比赛？

tf.q: 在中国，只有年轻人喜欢乒乓球运动。
1959年，乒乓球运动传入中国。
中国人只喜欢看自己国家的运动员比赛。

mc.q: 乒乓球是从（ ）传入中国的。
“乒乓球的重量虽然很轻，但是它在中国人心中却是很重很重的”，意思是（ ）。

很多中国人喜欢打乒乓球

tip.title: 中国人的国球
tip.zh: 乒乓球被称为中国的“国球”。1959年，容国团在第25届世界乒乓球锦标赛上获得男子单打冠军，这是中国运动员获得的第一个世界冠军。从那以后，中国乒乓球队培养了一大批优秀运动员，在世界比赛中取得了很好的成绩。乒乓球还在中美关系史上起过特别的作用：1971年，中国邀请美国乒乓球队访华，打开了两国交往的大门，第二年美国总统尼克松访问中国。人们把这件事叫做“乒乓外交”，说是“小球转动了大球”。
tip.en: Table tennis is known as China's “national ball game”. In 1959 Rong Guotuan won the men's singles at the 25th World Table Tennis Championships—the first world title ever won by a Chinese athlete. Since then the Chinese table tennis team has trained a great many outstanding players and achieved excellent results in world competitions. Table tennis also played a special role in the history of China–US relations: in 1971 China invited the American table tennis team to visit, opening the door to contact between the two countries, and the following year US President Nixon visited China. People call this “ping-pong diplomacy”, saying that “the little ball moved the big ball (the globe)”.

lessons.title: “三大件”的变化
lessons.daodu: 现在你通过什么来判断一个家庭的经济情况呢？汽车？房子？还是别的什么？如果是在30年前呢？
lessons.daoduEn: Today, how do you judge a family's financial situation? Its car? Its house? Or something else? And what about 30 years ago?

paras.zh: “三大件”对于今天的许多年轻人可能是个比较陌生的词汇，然而这个词却曾经是中国家庭生活水平和消费水平提高的重要标志。
paras.py: “Sān dà jiàn” duìyú jīntiān de xǔduō niánqīngrén kěnéng shì gè bǐjiào mòshēng de cíhuì, rán'ér zhège cí què céngjīng shì Zhōngguó jiātíng shēnghuó shuǐpíng hé xiāofèi shuǐpíng tígāo de zhòngyào biāozhì.
paras.en: "The Three Big Items" may be an unfamiliar term to many young people today, but it was once an important sign of rising living standards and spending power in Chinese families.

paras.zh: 在上个世纪70年代，“三大件”是手表、缝纫机、自行车，而电视这样的家用电器，对普通家庭来说还是很难想象的。到了80年代，“三大件”变成了彩电、冰箱、洗衣机。在生活还不富裕的年代，有好节目的时候，不少人会到有电视的邻居家去看电视。这样，电视就让人们聚到了一起。在90年代，“三大件”成了电话、电脑、空调。那时，一般家庭还买不起电脑，而今天电脑已经成了普通老百姓也买得起的普通电器了。这个变化仅仅用了不到20年的时间。到了21世纪的今天，“三大件”已经不再与家用电器有关，已经变成了住房、汽车和良好的子女教育。
paras.py: Zài shàng gè shìjì 70 niándài, “sān dà jiàn” shì shǒubiǎo, féngrènjī, zìxíngchē, ér diànshì zhèyàng de jiāyòng diànqì, duì pǔtōng jiātíng lái shuō hái shì hěn nán xiǎngxiàng de. Dàole 80 niándài, “sān dà jiàn” biànchéngle cǎidiàn, bīngxiāng, xǐyījī. Zài shēnghuó hái bú fùyù de niándài, yǒu hǎo jiémù de shíhou, bù shǎo rén huì dào yǒu diànshì de línjū jiā qù kàn diànshì. Zhèyàng, diànshì jiù ràng rénmen jùdàole yìqǐ. Zài 90 niándài, “sān dà jiàn” chéngle diànhuà, diànnǎo, kōngtiáo. Nà shí, yìbān jiātíng hái mǎi bu qǐ diànnǎo, ér jīntiān diànnǎo yǐjīng chéngle pǔtōng lǎobǎixìng yě mǎi de qǐ de pǔtōng diànqì le. Zhège biànhuà jǐnjǐn yòngle bú dào 20 nián de shíjiān. Dàole 21 shìjì de jīntiān, “sān dà jiàn” yǐjīng bú zài yǔ jiāyòng diànqì yǒuguān, yǐjīng biànchéngle zhùfáng, qìchē hé liánghǎo de zǐnǚ jiàoyù.
paras.en: In the 1970s, the "three big items" were a watch, a sewing machine and a bicycle; home appliances like TVs were still hard for ordinary families to even imagine. In the 1980s, they became a color TV, a fridge and a washing machine. In those years when life wasn't yet well-off, when there was a good program on, many people would go to a neighbor who had a TV to watch it. So TV brought people together. In the 1990s, the "three big items" became a telephone, a computer and an air conditioner. Back then, ordinary families couldn't afford computers, but today computers are common appliances that ordinary people can afford. This change took less than 20 years. Now, in the 21st century, the "three big items" no longer have anything to do with appliances: they have become a home, a car and a good education for one's children.

paras.zh: 从自行车到汽车，从电视到电脑，从解决基本穿戴问题到重视子女教育，“三大件”不断发生着新的变化。这种变化反映出几十年来中国人生活质量和生活观念的变化。
paras.py: Cóng zìxíngchē dào qìchē, cóng diànshì dào diànnǎo, cóng jiějué jīběn chuāndài wèntí dào zhòngshì zǐnǚ jiàoyù, “sān dà jiàn” búduàn fāshēngzhe xīn de biànhuà. Zhè zhǒng biànhuà fǎnyìng chū jǐ shí nián lái Zhōngguórén shēnghuó zhìliàng hé shēnghuó guānniàn de biànhuà.
paras.en: From bicycles to cars, from TVs to computers, from meeting basic needs for clothing to valuing children's education, the "three big items" keep changing. These changes reflect how Chinese people's quality of life and way of thinking about life have changed over the past few decades.

points.name: 买得（不）起
points.eg: 而今天电脑已经成了普通老百姓也买得起的普通电器了。
points.egEn: ...whereas today the computer has become an ordinary appliance that ordinary people can afford.
points.zh: “动词+得起/不起”是可能补语，表示有没有能力（多指经济能力）做某事，如“买得起、住不起、吃得起”。
points.enx: “Verb + 得起/不起” is a potential complement showing whether one can afford (usually financially) to do something, e.g. 买得起 (can afford to buy), 住不起 (can't afford to live in).
egs: （1）这里的房子太贵了，我买不起。
（2）现在很多年轻人都买得起汽车了。

points.name: 反映
points.eg: 这种变化反映出几十年来中国人生活质量和生活观念的变化。
points.egEn: These changes reflect the changes in Chinese people's quality of life and way of thinking over the past few decades.
points.zh: “反映”，动词，表示把客观情况表现出来，常用格式“反映出……”。也可以表示把情况或意见告诉上级或有关部门。
points.enx: “反映” means “to reflect; to mirror”—to show an objective situation, often in the pattern “反映出……”. It can also mean to report a situation or opinion to a higher authority.
egs: （1）这部电影反映了普通人的生活。
（2）学生们向学校反映了食堂的问题。

think: “三大件”是什么意思？不同的时代，它各有什么内容？
电视为什么可以把人们聚到一起？
“三大件”的变化说明了什么？

tip.title: 从凭票供应到应有尽有
tip.titleEn: From Coupon-Based Supply to Abundance of Everything
tip.zh: 从20世纪50年代到80年代，中国实行计划经济，很多生活用品不能随便买，要凭票供应。买粮食要用粮票，买布要用布票，买油、肉、糖等也都需要相应的票证。那时候，就算有钱，没有票也买不到东西。1978年改革开放以后，经济快速发展，商品越来越丰富，各种票证渐渐退出了历史舞台。到了20世纪90年代初，粮票也不再使用了。今天，商店和超市里的商品应有尽有，人们还可以在网上购物，生活发生了翻天覆地的变化。
tip.en: From the 1950s to the 1980s China had a planned economy, and many daily necessities could not be bought freely but were supplied only with coupons. Grain required grain coupons, cloth required cloth coupons, and oil, meat, sugar and so on also needed their own coupons. In those days, even if you had money, you couldn't buy anything without coupons. After reform and opening-up began in 1978, the economy developed rapidly, goods became more and more plentiful, and the coupons gradually passed into history; by the early 1990s even grain coupons were no longer used. Today shops and supermarkets have everything one could wish for, and people can also shop online—life has changed beyond recognition.

lessons.title: 下围棋的故事
lessons.daodu: 在中国古代，如果让皇帝生气，后果会很严重。看看那些将军们是怎么做的吧。
lessons.daoduEn: In ancient China, making the emperor angry could have very serious consequences. Let's see how one of his generals handled it.

paras.zh: 明朝的皇帝朱元璋和将军徐达从小就是好朋友，关系非常好。朱元璋很喜欢下围棋，不过他的水平一般。徐达也喜欢下围棋，他的水平比朱元璋要高得多。
paras.py: Míngcháo de huángdì Zhū Yuánzhāng hé jiāngjūn Xú Dá cóngxiǎo jiù shì hǎo péngyou, guānxi fēicháng hǎo. Zhū Yuánzhāng hěn xǐhuan xià wéiqí, búguò tā de shuǐpíng yìbān. Xú Dá yě xǐhuan xià wéiqí, tā de shuǐpíng bǐ Zhū Yuánzhāng yào gāo de duō.
paras.en: Zhu Yuanzhang, emperor of the Ming Dynasty, and General Xu Da had been good friends since childhood and were very close. Zhu Yuanzhang loved playing Go, but he was only an average player. Xu Da liked Go too, and he was much better at it than Zhu Yuanzhang.

paras.zh: 朱元璋经常找徐达一起下围棋。徐达是个明白人，他知道皇帝总是希望自己做什么事情都比别人好。所以每次下棋的时候，他总是故意输给皇帝，以便让皇帝高兴。
paras.py: Zhū Yuánzhāng jīngcháng zhǎo Xú Dá yìqǐ xià wéiqí. Xú Dá shì gè míngbairén, tā zhīdào huángdì zǒngshì xīwàng zìjǐ zuò shénme shìqing dōu bǐ biérén hǎo. Suǒyǐ měi cì xiàqí de shíhou, tā zǒngshì gùyì shū gěi huángdì, yǐbiàn ràng huángdì gāoxìng.
paras.en: Zhu Yuanzhang often asked Xu Da to play Go with him. Xu Da was a sensible man; he knew the emperor always wanted to be better than others at everything. So every time they played, he lost to the emperor on purpose to keep him happy.

paras.zh: 有一天，他们两个一起游玩，看到了一个漂亮的湖。朱元璋突然很想下棋，就对徐达说：“今天如果你能赢我，我就把这个湖奖给你。”
paras.py: Yǒu yì tiān, tāmen liǎng gè yìqǐ yóuwán, kàndàole yí gè piàoliang de hú. Zhū Yuánzhāng tūrán hěn xiǎng xiàqí, jiù duì Xú Dá shuō: “Jīntiān rúguǒ nǐ néng yíng wǒ, wǒ jiù bǎ zhège hú jiǎng gěi nǐ.”
paras.en: One day, the two of them went on an outing and came to a beautiful lake. Zhu Yuanzhang suddenly felt like playing Go and said to Xu Da: "If you can beat me today, I'll give you this lake as a prize."

paras.zh: 徐达点头同意了，但是心中很矛盾：如果自己赢了，皇帝一定会不高兴；可是如果输了，自己又舍不得这个湖。最后，他想出了一个办法，就开始认真地下棋。这次和平时不同，他丝毫也不让着皇帝，拿出所有的本领，赢了皇帝。朱元璋觉得丢了面子，正要生气，徐达说：“请您看一看棋盘。”
paras.py: Xú Dá diǎntóu tóngyì le, dànshì xīn zhōng hěn máodùn: Rúguǒ zìjǐ yíng le, huángdì yídìng huì bù gāoxìng; kěshì rúguǒ shū le, zìjǐ yòu shěbude zhège hú. Zuìhòu, tā xiǎng chūle yí gè bànfǎ, jiù kāishǐ rènzhēn de xiàqí. Zhè cì hé píngshí bù tóng, tā sīháo yě bú ràngzhe huángdì, náchū suǒyǒu de běnlǐng, yíngle huángdì. Zhū Yuánzhāng juéde diūle miànzi, zhèng yào shēngqì, Xú Dá shuō: “Qǐng nín kàn yi kàn qípán.”
paras.en: Xu Da nodded in agreement, but he was torn: if he won, the emperor would surely be unhappy; but if he lost, he would hate to give up the lake. In the end he thought of a plan and began playing seriously. Unlike other times, he didn't let the emperor win at all; he used all his skill and beat him. Zhu Yuanzhang felt he had lost face and was about to get angry when Xu Da said: "Please take a look at the board."

paras.zh: 朱元璋低头一看，发现棋盘上的棋子看起来好像“万岁”两个字。他立刻笑了，觉得徐达的水平确实很高，对他更加佩服。于是，朱元璋就把湖奖给了徐达，还为他建了一座楼，名叫“胜棋楼”。
paras.py: Zhū Yuánzhāng dī tóu yí kàn, fāxiàn qípán shang de qízǐ kàn qǐlai hǎoxiàng “wànsuì” liǎng gè zì. Tā lìkè xiào le, juéde Xú Dá de shuǐpíng quèshí hěn gāo, duì tā gèngjiā pèifú. Yúshì, Zhū Yuánzhāng jiù bǎ hú jiǎng gěile Xú Dá, hái wèi tā jiànle yí zuò lóu, míng jiào “Shèngqí Lóu”.
paras.en: Zhu Yuanzhang looked down and saw that the stones on the board seemed to form the two characters 万岁 wànsuì ("long live the emperor"). He laughed at once, feeling that Xu Da really was a superb player, and admired him even more. So Zhu Yuanzhang gave the lake to Xu Da and also built him a tower called the "Shengqi Lou" (Tower of the Winning Game).

points.name: 以便
points.eg: 所以每次下棋的时候，他总是故意输给皇帝，以便让皇帝高兴。
points.egEn: So every time they played, he would always lose to the emperor on purpose, so as to make the emperor happy.
points.zh: “以便”，连词，用在后一个分句的开头，表示前面所说的做法是为了让后面的目的更容易实现，多用于书面语。
points.enx: “以便” is a conjunction meaning “so as to; in order that”. It begins the second clause, showing that the action before it is meant to make the purpose after it easier to achieve. It is mostly used in written Chinese.
egs: （1）请把你的地址写下来，以便我们给你寄资料。
（2）他每天早上听中文广播，以便提高自己的听力水平。

points.name: 让
points.eg: 他丝毫也不让着皇帝，拿出所有的本领，赢了皇帝。
points.egEn: He didn't give way to the emperor in the slightest; he used all his skill and beat the emperor.
points.zh: “让”，动词，在这里表示把好处或方便留给别人，比如比赛时故意不拿出全部本领，常说“让着某人”。
points.enx: Here “让” is a verb meaning “to give way; to let someone have the advantage”, e.g. deliberately not playing at full strength in a game. It is often used as “让着 + someone”.
egs: （1）他是你弟弟，你应该让着他一点儿。
（2）下棋的时候，爸爸从来不让我，所以我总是输。

tip.title: 皇帝与“万岁”
tip.zh: “皇帝”这个称号是从秦始皇开始的。公元前221年，秦王嬴政统一了中国，他认为自己的功劳比古代的“三皇五帝”还大，于是称自己为“皇帝”。“万岁”本来是人们表示庆祝和祝福的话，意思是活一万年。后来，这个词渐渐成为对皇帝的专门称呼，大臣见到皇帝时要说“万岁，万岁，万万岁”，普通人不能随便使用。课文里徐达用棋子摆出“万岁”两个字，就是巧妙地表达了对皇帝的尊敬。
tip.en: The title “huangdi” (emperor) began with the First Emperor of Qin. In 221 BC, King Ying Zheng of Qin unified China. Believing his achievements were even greater than those of the legendary “Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors” of ancient times, he called himself “huangdi”. “Wansui” was originally an expression of celebration and good wishes, meaning “live ten thousand years”. Later the word gradually became a form of address reserved for the emperor: ministers meeting the emperor had to say “Long live, long live, long live the emperor!”, and ordinary people could not use it casually. In the text, Xu Da arranged his Go stones into the characters “wansui”—a clever way of showing respect for the emperor.
